aichat.task: get a concrete task done with an AI chat assistant (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot): pose a real task — draft an email, plan a trip, summarize a document, write or fix something, generate an image — iterate on the response at least once, and end with a usable result; complete when the refined result is on screen and accepted (copied, downloaded, or applied). Surface pinned: the assistant's own chat interface — not news about AI, not prompt-tips listicles without a live session.

tree.label: Complete a task with an AI assistant
tree.note: 1 then 2, with 2's walls interleaving wherever the platform puts them; 3 sends the ask; 4 judges what came back; 5 loops back into 3 or 4 until an output passes - one pass through that loop is enough for the task to count as done in this domain; 6 extracts and lands the result; in a multi-tool chain the landed output of 6 becomes the next tool's input material in 3.3, and the whole of 3-6 repeats per tool

children.label: Reach the assistant
children.note: 1.1 then 1.3; 1.2 before anything installs or signs in when the route came through search or a store; 1.4 whenever a wall comes up - permissions, consent, intro modals

amazon.task: buy a physical product on Amazon: search for an item, work the results list, open and assess a product page (price, rating, variant options, delivery date), add to cart, and check out; complete when the order confirmation or the final checkout review screen with the order total is on screen. Surface pinned: Amazon's own website or app — not a third-party wrapper or assistive shopping app, not a haul/unboxing video, not a deals-roundup or affiliate-listicle without a live purchase session. Variants: returns and refunds (see returns), reordering a past purchase (see reorder), leaving a review (see review), and Amazon Fresh grocery orders (see groceries) do not belong.

animation.task: create an animation in an animation tool (Canva animate, After Effects, CapCut, Alight Motion, PowerPoint morph): animate a concrete element — a text animation, logo reveal, or keyframed/preset motion — preview it, and export; complete when the export finishes or the final animation plays back inside the session. apartment.task: search for an apartment and contact the listing (Zillow, Apartments.com, Trulia): set location, price, and bedroom filters, evaluate listings and their trustworthiness, pick candidates, send an inquiry or tour request; complete when the inquiry-sent or tour-request confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: an apartment-listing website or app. Variants: submitting a rental application with documents, roommate finding, and buying a home do not belong.

tree.label: Find a rental apartment
tree.note: do 1. 2 only as the account state demands - 9tEl registers before anything else, most keepers arrive signed in and skip it, and 8.2 reaches into 2.5 when a save hits the login wall (dS5q). repeat 3, 4, and 5 in any order until the results fit: 5.1's count drives the revisions (9tEl, mKVE, n9qo), and 3.4 or 3.5 re-cut the set as silently as any filter. 5.6 opens 6 - except on 3.3, which lands inside 6 directly and reaches 5 only by backing out (iHOh). from 6: back to 5 for the next candidate (pCy8, mKVE, Q8ex), into 7 to prepare contact, into 8 to keep it - in any order, or not at all. no keeper carries 7 past 7.5. 8.6 and 8.7 close the loop on 8's own actions.

children.label: Reach the rental search
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2. 1.3 whenever the platform lands on the for-sale side - at entry (4NIC, XmWM), inside the search sheet (7oPn), or as a check that finds nothing wrong (n9qo). 1.4 and 1.5 as they come up.

questions.question: Is the result about to be opened the official Zillow site rather than a sponsored ad or a third-party lookalike?
questions.why: Selecting the top result titled 'Zillow: Real Estate, Apartments, Mortgages & Home Values' ensures you navigate to the legitimate platform rather than a sponsored ad or third-party site.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify they are entering the authentic, secure real estate marketplace rather than a potentially deceptive link.

questions.question: Which option under the Rent menu matches the ask?
questions.why: The 'Rent' dropdown menu offers different starting points like apartments, houses, or all rentals, which sets the baseline property filter for your search.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to immediately narrow the search strictly to apartments instead of having to sift through single-family homes and other property types.

questions.question: Are the search results showing rentals for your chosen zip code?
questions.why: The screen displays '[address] Listings' and an active 'For Rent' filter, which confirms the base search parameters are correct before you add more specific filters.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to visually confirm that the agent is searching in the correct area and hasn't accidentally included properties for sale.

questions.question: Is the search set to For rent or For sale?
questions.why: The interface defaults to the 'For sale' tab, which will show homes to buy instead of apartments to lease if left unchanged.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify that the fundamental search category matches their specific housing needs.

questions.question: A notice is covering the results and it changes how the price is read - what does it say, before it is dismissed?
questions.why: The site is displaying a 'Say hello to total monthly price' modal that overlays the 26,075 available Los Angeles rentals and needs to be cleared to interact with the page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to read and understand how the platform calculates and displays the total monthly price before the notice is dismissed.

questions.question: What language is the site set to?
questions.why: The dropdown menu displays multiple language options like Español and 简体中文, which determines the language used for the search interface and listing details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent defaults to English without asking, you lose the opportunity to navigate the site and read apartment details in your preferred language.

children.label: Sign in or register
children.note: 2.1; 2.2 to 2.4 only on a first run (9tEl). 2.5 fires mid-task, entered from 8.2, when a save demands an account (dS5q). most keepers arrive signed in and the whole goal is a no-op.

billpay.task: pay a bill through a bank or biller portal (bank bill pay, utility, credit-card, phone-company sites): log in, locate the bill or add the payee, set the amount and payment date, pick the funding account, submit; complete when the payment-scheduled or payment-confirmed screen is on screen. Surface pinned: a bank's bill-pay interface or a biller's own web/app payment portal. Variants: setting up recurring autopay, sending money to a person, and paying at a store register do not belong.

tree.label: Pay a bill online
tree.note: 1 where the session is not already inside - half the keepers arrive signed in. then 2. 3 on the bill-pay and wallet surfaces, where the payee has to be found, linked or typed; on the issuer sites the To field is the user's own card or loan and 3 is skipped. 4 before 5, though on the wallet surfaces the bill is read at the form itself. 5, then 6 - or 6 first where the source has to be linked before anything (EnZK), or 6.2 mid-way when the picked account turns out unverified (W0JT). 7 where the platform offers dates and rails; on the wallets the money leaves at once, so 7 is only reading what the platform prints. then 8, then 9. 9.7 loops back to 2 for the next bill - three times in 8n6j.

children.note: 1.1 where the video starts outside the app or site, then 1.2; 1.3 whenever the platform interrupts. 1.4 once, on a bank whose bill pay is not yet enrolled (NfKb) or a tool that charges for it (W0JT). 1.5 in place of 1.2 on a biller portal that has never seen the user (RoGB) - the login page offers sign in, register, or a one-time payment by account number, and the first visit takes register.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the peace of mind of personally verifying that the authentic, non-sponsored bank link was chosen to avoid phishing risks.

questions.question: Will you type your bank username and password in yourself?
questions.why: The login page requires a username and password to proceed with the selected passcode table method.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user must share their sensitive banking credentials with the agent to allow it to log in.

questions.question: Will you choose and type the new password the site now requires?
questions.why: The portal requires you to create a new 4-6 digit password before you can finish logging in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose a memorable, secure password that you alone know for future access to this account.

questions.question: Do you want to extend your banking session before it times out?
questions.why: The screen displays a 60-second warning that your session will expire for security reasons unless you choose to continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to quickly intervene to keep the session active, risking a timeout and lost progress if the agent misses the brief warning window.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read and understand the specific legal terms, rights, and responsibilities you are legally binding yourself to.

questions.question: Which bill-pay plan do you want, given each one is a monthly charge?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose the subscription tier that best balances the monthly fee with your expected payment volume.

questions.question: Are the business name and address on the form the ones you gave me?

questions.why: The form requires sensitive personal details, including the last 4 digits of your SSN and your date of birth, to verify your identity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step removes your ability to control exactly when and where your highly sensitive personal information is shared for underwriting purposes.

EnZK runs 2.4 twice, before and after 6.2.

cad.task: model a part in parametric CAD software (Fusion 360, Onshape, Tinkercad, SketchUp, FreeCAD, Shapr3D): pick a plane and draw a sketch, constrain and dimension it so the geometry is defined rather than eyeballed, turn it into a solid by extruding or revolving, add the features the part needs — fillets, chamfers, holes, shells, patterns — measure or check fit against the dimensions it has to hit, and export it for manufacture as STL, STEP, or a dimensioned drawing; complete when the export completes or the finished part is shown fully defined. Surface pinned: the modelling session on one part. This domain differs from the rest of the creative set in that the work has a correctness condition, not only a look: a dimension is right or wrong, a sketch is fully constrained or it is not, and parts either fit or they do not. Capture that. Off-task: rendering, materials and lighting passes, animation or exploded-view videos, digital sculpting for art (Blender, ZBrush), slicer-only walkthroughs that start from a downloaded STL, 3D-printer reviews and calibration, and software overviews that never build one part.

tree.label: Model and export a CAD part
tree.note: 1 first, and its units and its component constrain everything after. 2 wherever the part has to match something real, which is eight of the seventeen, and it can run before the first sketch or in the middle. then 3, 4 and 5 as one loop, once per feature: rglv runs it three times, N3Dw eight. 6 as the part needs, and 6.11 wherever one feature has to repeat. 7 whenever an earlier value turns out wrong, which is every parametric video and none of the three SketchUp ones. 8 when there is something to check against, and 9 last. LVhh, YFgd and zmd0 never reach 9 at all, and A5bc stops before 6 and says so.

children.label: Set up the modelling session
children.note: 1.9 first where the tool is not on the machine yet, which is rglv alone. then 1.1 and 1.2 before any geometry, in that order - A5bc, 4G2E, 6yPK, d3qG, zmd0 and N3Dw all set the units first, and pMWn instead attaches a unit to each dimension in 4.4. 1.3 where the tutorial wants a known starting state. 1.4 and 1.5 before the first sketch in the course videos and never in the SketchUp ones. 1.6, 1.7 and 1.8 whenever the screen gets in the way, and they are revisited: LVhh runs 1.8 four times and YFgd runs it at the end for the final shot.

LVhh, YFgd and zmd0 never save or export at all, and their tasks end on a finished-looking model instead.

calendly.task: land a meeting time with another person through a scheduling tool (Calendly, Doodle, Microsoft Bookings): open the invite link — or set up the event/poll and get it answered — compare availability, pick a slot, confirm; complete when the meeting-confirmed screen, or the poll's agreed final time, is on screen with the event details. Either side of the handshake belongs as long as the recording reaches a confirmed time. Surface pinned: a scheduling tool on the web. Variants: emailing back and forth about times, plain calendar-event creation with no counterparty, and configuring availability settings without a resulting booking do not belong.

tree.label: Schedule a meeting with others
tree.note: do 1. 2, 3, 4 in the order the tool's wizard dictates - Doodle and Outlook describe first (eZyb, W0fS), Google Calendar sets the rules first and takes the description on page two (VKIQ); 5.1 comes before 3 in the mail family, because the poll pane stays disabled until someone is on the To line and the availability icons need those names (VxrV, KbIz). then 5. 6 happens on the other side of the link - nine keepers cross over, always by simulating the invitee. 7 on poll routes only: booking routes commit at 6.5.4, and when2meet stops at the heatmap with no close at all (ythO). 8 interleaves from the first committed change - holds are checked minutes after sending (VxrV), rule edits are checked by refreshing the public page mid-setup (6Pzf). 9 when the offer needs editing and re-sharing, or taking down.

children.label: Get into the scheduling tool
children.note: 1.1 and 1.2 on web arrivals from search (udxi, X48l, 6Yg3); 1.3 once, on the desktop add-in (KbIz). 1.4 as the account state demands - most keepers arrive signed in, one goes guest, one registers from nothing, and Doodle lets creation start first and injects the wall mid-flow (MVu8, udxi). 1.5 whenever a nag interrupts. then 1.6 and 1.7; 1.8 where a first run offers it (VKIQ).

cancelsub.task: cancel a subscription (Netflix, gym and streaming services, app-store subscriptions): sign in, find the buried cancel path in account settings — or the phone's subscription manager — click through the retention offers, confirm; complete when the cancellation confirmation showing the service end date is on screen. Surface pinned: the service's website/app account settings or the phone's subscription-manager screen. Variants: pausing or downgrading a plan, deleting the account entirely, and disputing a charge do not belong.

carinsurance.task: get a car-insurance quote online and proceed toward buying the policy: enter vehicle and driver details, choose coverage options and deductibles, review the quote price, and continue toward purchase; complete when a priced quote (or a purchase confirmation) is on screen. Surface pinned: an insurer's quote website or app (GEICO, Progressive, State Farm, Allstate, Root). Variants: insurance-agent sales training, "cheapest insurance" talking-head advice, and claims filing do not belong.

tree.note: do 1, then 2 - the route in 2 decides how much of 3, 4 and 5 the site asks: BCare asks none of 3 and 4 after the sequence number, GEICO already holds the car and the licence. 3, 4 and 5 in the site's own order, one page each on Progressive and one question per screen on GEICO. 6 sits where the site puts the contact gate - before any price on PolicyBazaar and GEICO, after the whole form on Progressive and Compare the Market, nowhere on The Zebra and BCare. 7 and 8 loop on one page until the figure is right - on the aggregators 7.1, 7.4 and 7.7 are asked before the price and 8 follows once. then 9; 9.1 comes before 6 on BCare and Compare the Market. one keeper reaches 9.10, and eight stop at a different point in 9.

classreg.task: register for a class through a school's registration portal (university and community-college student portals, community-ed sites): search the course catalog, check open seats and schedule fit, add the course to the cart or schedule, enroll and pay if required; complete when the enrolled schedule or registration confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: a web registration portal. Variants: applying for admission, financial-aid forms, and buying self-paced MOOC courses (Udemy, Coursera) do not belong.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the creative control to visually balance and size the text exactly how you want it on the background shape.

questions.question: Is there a second blank bookmark on the canvas?
questions.why: The context menu displays multiple clipboard actions, and choosing 'Duplicate' directly clones the selected shape onto the canvas.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step removes your control over deciding exactly how many identical items to produce in the final cut.

questions.question: How should you create the background shadow layer?
questions.why: The right-click menu provides a Duplicate option that allows you to create an identical shape to manually offset as a shadow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the creative control of manually dragging and positioning the duplicated layer to achieve the exact visual offset you want.

questions.question: Are the letters and the heart welded into one cut path?
questions.why: Combining the individual text and heart layers into a single 'Weld Result' layer ensures the machine cuts the design as one continuous piece instead of slicing through overlapping shapes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly which overlapping elements should be permanently merged into a single silhouette.

questions.question: Why do you weld the thin rectangle to the top edge of the brick wall?
questions.why: The screen shows the rectangle being merged with the wall to create a thicker, sturdier base that can physically support the other design elements.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to structurally reinforce specific parts of the design based on the physical weight and assembly requirements of the final craft.

questions.question: Which layers do you select to slice the first letter?
questions.why: Selecting the specific 'Text - Impact' layer and the 'Print Then Cut' photo layer ensures the slice tool cuts the image into the exact shape of that letter.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the creative control of deciding exactly which part of the photo is sliced into which specific letter of your design.

questions.question: Is the photo sliced into the second letter, with a Slice Result for it?
questions.why: Selecting both the photo and the specific text layer in the Layers panel enables the Slice tool to cut the image into that exact shape.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the creative control of deciding exactly which letter shapes to slice the photo into and verifying the resulting layers.

questions.question: Do the Slice Result layers show the letters cut out of the image?
questions.why: Checking the 'Slice Result' layers in the panel and moving the top image ensures the software actually cut the desired shapes out of the photo.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual confirmation and quality control of moving the original photo aside to ensure the sliced letters look exactly the way you want.

questions.question: Which leftover layers from the slice operation should you delete?
questions.why: The layers panel shows multiple slice results, and failing to delete the original text outlines and photo will cause the machine to cut or draw unwanted elements.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing the ability to manually verify that only the correct photo-filled letters remain for the final project.

questions.question: Which elements of the design should you apply an offset to next?
questions.why: The canvas displayed multiple letters, and selecting specific ones determines which parts of the design receive the offset effect.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses creative control over which specific elements of their design are highlighted with an offset.

questions.question: What size should the offset outline be?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to visually balance the thickness of the outline against the rest of your specific design.

questions.question: Do you want to use the Contour tool to hide the small artifacts in the welded layer?
questions.why: The canvas showed unwanted small spots in the green layer, and hiding them ensures a clean cut without tiny holes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually inspect the design for tiny imperfections and decide exactly which artifacts to hide.

questions.question: How do you want to create a solid base layer from the outline?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the creative control to decide whether to completely fill the silhouette or leave specific internal cut lines visible for your base layer.

children.label: Assign layers to the machine
children.note: 4.1 where a layer should draw, print or cut differently from its default - and Pen so the image under a layer stays visible before 3.6. 4.2 on every layer that will cut from its own material; the colour decides which mat each layer lands on in 6. 4.3 on a print layer, 4.4 on a cut layer that must hold its place, and both on a kiss-cut sheet. 4.5 last, before 6 - a hidden layer does not cut, so any layer hidden during the design must be shown again if it needs to cut.

questions.question: Are your layers set to the correct operation types for cutting versus printing?
questions.why: Selecting 'Basic Cut' or 'Print Then Cut' in the operation dropdown ensures the machine correctly distinguishes the artwork to be printed from the lines to be cut.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the direct oversight of assigning specific physical operations to each individual layer of their design.

questions.question: Are the faces where you want them inside the letters before the slice?

questions.question: What color do you want the text to be?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the creative choice to visually coordinate the text color with specific elements of your design.

questions.question: Do the new text's size and colour match what this project needs?
questions.why: The screen shows the text being resized with the bounding box and recolored via the Operation menu to match the project's scale and material needs.

questions.question: Are the draw and cut actions correctly combined on a single mat in the preview?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual reassurance of seeing your drawn text and cut shape properly aligned on the same virtual mat before committing to the job.

questions.question: Which template layers should you hide to reduce clutter before decorating?

children.label: Size the design to fit
children.note: the user measures the object in 5.1, before or after the design, whenever a real object sets the size - a blank, a garment, a mug, a board. 5.2 where a template or a stand-in shape shows how the design fits on the object. in 5.3 the user sets the final dimensions. then the machine's limits: 5.4 when a warning names a maximum, 5.5 when the design is bigger than any mat, 5.6 is for using the whole sheet, and 5.7 for making sure the pieces cut as separate pieces. 6.4 sends the user back here when a piece spills onto another mat.

questions.question: What dimensions should you use for the design based on the physical item?

questions.question: What size is the physical garment you are designing for?

questions.question: What specific dimensions do you want to resize the text box to?

questions.question: Did the size set earlier already put this over the cutting limit?
questions.why: The stencil width of 14.056 inches shown at 09:01 directly explains the software's warning at 11:25 that the image exceeds the standard 11.5-inch cutting area.

questions.question: Should you click OK to use a larger mat or cancel to reduce the image size?

questions.question: How do you size the template shape to match the maximum printable area?
questions.why: Unlocking the padlock icon and entering exact width and height values ensures the slicing template perfectly matches the software's print-then-cut limits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the hands-on control of defining the exact slicing boundaries to optimize how your specific design fits within the print-then-cut constraints.

questions.question: Are you using the material efficiently?
questions.why: The mat preview shows a large empty space within the restricted cutting area, indicating that material will be wasted if cut as-is.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to specify exactly how many identical sticker sheets to produce based on your current material supply and project needs.

questions.question: Are the white borders of your stickers overlapping?
questions.why: Placing a temporary dark grey square behind the images makes their white borders visible so you can ensure the cut lines do not intersect.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to visually verify the exact spacing of the white borders to guarantee a clean, separate cut for each sticker.

questions.question: Were the stickers placed by hand where the replication tools would be safer?
questions.why: A physical printed sheet of stickers demonstrates that automated row and column replication ensures perfect alignment for the machine's sensors, except for very small stickers which require manual placement to avoid cutting errors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to apply nuanced, experience-based judgment about when a design is small enough to require manual placement instead of automated alignment tools.

children.label: Prepare the mats
children.note: 6.1 where the user needs to save the project - in two recordings the user saves the project, and in one the user chooses not to. 6.2 covers what the user checks before clicking Make It. on newer versions the user goes through 6.3 first. the user goes through 6.4 on every run, and it sends the user back to 3, 4 or 5 whenever the preview is wrong - in seven of the recordings the user cancels here at least once. 6.5 where the paper or the mat is not the default. for an iron-on, infusible-ink or sublimation job the user goes through 6.6 on every mat, and skips it for a sticker, decal or stencil job. then 7 for a print job, else 8.

questions.question: Was the document closed without saving on purpose, with nothing you wanted lost?
questions.why: Clicking the close 'x' on the document tab triggers a dialog box asking if you want to save your changes before closing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to intentionally discard unwanted modifications to keep your files unaltered before clearing the workspace.

questions.question: What do you want to name the project, and should it be saved as public?
questions.why: The save dialog requires a project name and includes a checkbox that determines if the design is shared publicly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose control over your project's organization and whether your personal design is shared with the public.

questions.question: Does the software block the cut and prompt for payment because a premium element was accidentally left in the design?
questions.why: Cricut Design Space allows users to design with premium fonts and images but halts the process at the 'Make It' screen to demand payment or a subscription.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The ability to catch unexpected charges and choose to go back to the canvas to swap the premium element for a free alternative.

questions.question: Are you ready to send the design to the machine?
questions.why: Clicking the green 'Make It' button confirms your canvas arrangement and transitions the project to the mat preparation screen.

questions.question: How will you load your materials for this project?
questions.why: The software requires you to specify whether the materials will be loaded on a mat, without a mat, or in multiple ways to properly prepare the cut job.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the software's load method matches the physical materials and equipment you actually have on hand.

questions.question: How should you set the material load type for the second layer?
questions.why: Selecting "Without Mat" from the dropdown triggers a warning that your material must be at least 15 cm in length, which dictates how you physically prepare the vinyl.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that your physical piece of Smart Vinyl meets the specific length requirement displayed in the software's warning.

questions.question: Do the mat layout, material size, and mirror settings look correct before you continue?
questions.why: Reviewing the layout, the 4.5" x 6.5" material size, and the mirror setting ensures the design will cut properly on your physical material.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the virtual mat layout perfectly matches the physical piece of material you plan to load into the machine.

questions.question: Which layer do you want to cut first?

questions.question: Are the material sizes set correctly for your print and cut mats?
questions.why: The screen shows material size options for each mat, which must match your physical materials so the machine cuts within the correct boundaries.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to ensure the software's mat sizes perfectly match the specific physical materials you have on hand.

questions.question: Is the Cameo 4 the machine you actually have connected?
questions.why: The Page Setup panel showed the media size set to A4 and the machine set to Cameo 4, which dictates the physical boundaries for your design.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the virtual canvas matches the exact physical material you plan to load into the machine.

questions.question: Do you need to mirror the design for this cut?
questions.why: Toggling the mirror switch flips the text in the preview so that the physical cut does not turn out backwards.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the manual check to ensure the design is properly mirrored for your specific transfer material.

questions.question: Do you need to flip the design horizontally for application on the inside of a transparent surface?
questions.why: The "Flip Horizontal" option in the top toolbar allows you to reverse the image so it appears correctly when viewed from the outside of a clear object.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to determine if your specific physical application requires a mirrored cut to display correctly.

children.label: Print the sheet
children.note: this goal applies only to a print then cut job, which is 13 of the recordings. on Silhouette 7.1 comes first, in Page Setup, and 7.3 is File then Print before 8. on Cricut the marks are automatic and 7.3 is Send to Printer on the Make screen after 6. the user goes through 7.2 whenever the layout gets close to the registration marks. the user goes through 7.4, then 7.5 only if the system-dialog switch in 7.4 is on. 7.6 happens before printing and 7.7 after the sheet is printed. if the sheet is already printed, the user picks I have already printed to skip this goal.

questions.question: How small should you set the registration mark insets to maximize the usable area on the sticker paper?
questions.why: Setting the insets to their minimum value of 0.394 inches pushes the registration marks to the very edges of the page setup screen, maximizing the space available for your designs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually maximize the printable area to fit as many stickers as possible on a single sheet.

questions.question: Do you want to turn on registration marks for your design?
questions.why: Enabling registration marks in the panel adds alignment guides to the virtual mat, which dictates the safe printable and cuttable area for a print-and-cut project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether the project should be formatted as a print-and-cut job with specific alignment boundaries.

questions.question: Does the layout fit correctly within the registration marks on your chosen material size?
questions.why: Checking the preview ensures your designs fit properly inside the black registration rectangle on the 8.5" x 11" material so the machine can read the marks and cut accurately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of visually confirming that the virtual layout perfectly matches your physical paper before committing to the print and cut.

questions.question: Does the outline box reach the sheet's corners?

questions.question: Are the print preview and printer settings correct for your design?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step removes your ability to visually verify the final print layout and ensure your preferred local printer is selected.

questions.question: Are bleed and the system dialog set the way this print needs?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to prevent unnecessary ink usage for bleeds or to apply custom quality settings specific to your physical printer.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visual confirmation that the bleed was successfully applied to the print file, which is crucial for preventing unwanted white borders on the final physical cut.

questions.question: Do you want to set the paper type and print quality for the sticker paper?
questions.why: Toggling the system dialog on allows you to change the media type from plain paper to a photo setting and increase the print quality to high.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually ensure the printed design has the optimal ink saturation and resolution for your specific physical materials.

questions.question: Should this second sheet print at High Quality, like the first one?
questions.why: Although you stated you were using the same settings, the on-screen print dialog shows the quality is set lower than the previous job.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance of consistent print quality across their project pieces when the agent fails to verify that the dialog settings match the intended ones.

questions.question: Does the print dialog's paper type match the transfer paper you're using?

questions.question: Are the material and pressure settings correct for this mat?
questions.why: The screen shows the material set to Light Cardstock and prompts for the Fine-Point Blade, which must match the physical material you are using to ensure a successful cut.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify that the software's material and tool settings match the physical materials you are about to load into the machine.

questions.question: Which material setting does the panel show selected, and does it match the material you're actually cutting?
questions.why: Selecting the correct cardstock weight from the search results ensures the machine applies enough pressure to cut through both the vinyl and its backing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to apply your personal experience regarding which specific material setting yields the best die-cut for your exact sticker paper.

questions.question: Does the material selected in the software match what's actually loaded?
questions.why: The software was set to Premium Vinyl - Permanent Glossy while the physical packaging showed Smart Vinyl Permanent Vinyl Shimmer, which could result in incorrect cut pressure.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to calibrate the exact cut pressure required for your specific physical materials and desired sticker style.

questions.why: Doing a test cut ensures the machine's pressure settings are correctly calibrated for a new or unfamiliar material, preventing you from ruining a full sheet.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the physical opportunity to verify the cut depth on a small scrap before committing the full sheet of material to the job.

questions.question: Should this material and pressure setting be remembered and applied to the remaining mats?
questions.why: Selecting the correct base material ensures the machine uses the right pressure, and checking the remember settings box saves time when processing multiple mats.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to specify the exact material type and decide whether to apply that setting universally to save time.

questions.why: The software prompts you to load a 'Fine-Point Blade', which creates a confusing discrepancy with the 'Premium Fine-Point Blade' listed on the physical box.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the human ability to deduce that the software's generic blade prompt safely corresponds to the premium blade included in the box.

questions.question: Which cutting blade should you choose for a design with fine details?
questions.why: The screen indicates the Knife Blade is best for moderate detail no smaller than three-quarters of an inch, meaning a different blade is required to successfully cut finer details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate the physical intricacies of your specific design against the hardware capabilities of each blade type.

questions.question: What material setting should you select on the machine's dial?
questions.why: Setting the physical dial to the correct material ensures the machine applies the appropriate blade pressure for the specific project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the physical control of manually turning the machine's dial to match the exact material they are loading.

children.label: Load and cut
children.note: for each mat the user goes through 9.1, 9.2 and 9.3 in order - to start the cut the user presses the machine's button, or SEND on Silhouette, or Go in the phone app. in 9.4 the user watches while the machine reads the marks and cuts. in three recordings the user goes through 9.5 before 9.6, and presses Go again if a corner has not cut. 9.6 closes the mat and moves the software to the next one or to Done; for a kiss-cut sheet the user goes through 6 again without printing again. in 25 of the 26 recordings the user goes through 9.7 outside the software after the last mat.

questions.question: Is your cutting machine connected and ready to receive the cut job?
questions.why: Seeing the green 'Ready' status next to your specific machine ensures the hardware is communicating properly before you click the blue 'SEND' button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss the final opportunity to verify the physical machine's connection status before committing your materials to the cut.

questions.question: Do you wait for the cutting progress circle to reach 100%?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to monitor the real-time cutting progress and intervene if the machine stalls.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to visually verify that the machine's sensor correctly detects the physical registration marks before it begins cutting the material.

children.label: Finish the object
children.note: these steps happen outside the software and on camera in 25 of the 26 recordings. the task in TASK.txt ends before them. for every cut the user goes through 9.7.1 and then 9.7.2. the next steps depend on the project: 9.7.3 and 9.7.4 for a decal or a stencil, 9.7.5 to 9.7.7 for iron-on, Infusible Ink and sublimation, 9.7.8 after a stencil is applied. 9.7.9 where pieces are glued, trimmed or fitted with hardware. 9.7.10 is the last step in every recording that shows the project completed.

questions.question: What heat settings and procedure does the guide show for this material?
questions.why: The screen details critical application instructions like 'Medium 25 s' and 'Light pressure' needed to properly adhere the iron-on design to the cotton.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to familiarize yourself with the specific heating times, pressure, and peeling instructions required to successfully finish your physical craft.

creditcard.task: apply for a credit card online as a consumer: open the card's apply page, fill the application (personal info, income, SSN-type identity fields), review disclosures and terms, submit, and see the decision or "under review" state; complete when the application-submitted or decision screen is on screen. Surface pinned: a bank or card issuer's website or app (Chase, Discover, Capital One, Amex, Citi, Bank of America). Variants: "best credit cards" rankings and reviews, credit-repair content, activating or using a card, and business payment-processing (merchant) content do not belong.

deleteacct.task: permanently delete an online account (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, any service): find the buried deletion path in settings or the privacy/GDPR data-deletion request page, verify identity or re-enter the password, acknowledge what will be lost, confirm; complete when the deletion-confirmed screen — or deletion-scheduled with its grace-period date — is on screen. Surface pinned: the service's website or app settings. Variants: temporary deactivation, unsubscribing from marketing emails, and cancelling a paid subscription do not belong.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty of knowing exactly when your data is permanently erased from the platform.

questions.question: After confirming deletion, does the screen show you logged out with a blank default photo?
questions.why: Visually confirming the logged-out state on the main feed proves the deletion request was successfully processed rather than silently failing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the guarantee that their account was actually deleted if the agent assumes success without verifying the final logged-out screen.

questions.question: After the final tap, did you see a deletion-confirmed screen, or did it just stay loading?
questions.why: The video cuts off while the final 'Delete account' button is still showing a loading spinner, leaving the actual success of the deletion unconfirmed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that the deletion request actually went through successfully rather than timing out or failing.

questions.question: After the deletion, does the account switcher list one fewer account than before?
questions.why: The frame at 1:05 only shows a phone held in a hand rather than the account switcher, making it impossible to visually confirm that the account count decreased from two to one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses definitive visual proof that the specific account was successfully removed from the device's active accounts list.

questions.question: Is your account permanently deleted immediately, or is there a grace period to recover it?
questions.why: The login screen explicitly states you have 30 days to log back in and recover your account, meaning the deletion is not immediately permanent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss seeing the exact 30-day deadline and instructions for recovering your account if you change your mind.

devicesetup.task: set up a new device through its companion app or on-device flow: a new phone (setup, account sign-in, data transfer), a router or mesh Wi-Fi via its app, a smartwatch pairing, or a smart-home device (camera, plug, speaker, doorbell): the unbox-to-working arc — pair or connect, sign in, configure the essentials; complete when the device shows working/connected in the app or the phone reaches its fully set-up home screen. Surface pinned: the setup flow itself — not unboxing-only or review videos.

tree.label: Set up a new device
tree.note: do 1, then 2. phone routes then do 3 and 4, where 4.3 is the whole of 4. accessory routes do 4 first, then 2.5 to 2.8, then 3 - the app will not look for a device until it knows the account. then 5 where anything is carried over; uSN0 and DT4C's first pass skip it outright. then 6. 7 always, and 7.9 when 7 comes back wrong. 8 on the transfer routes, reaching into 1.10 where the erase is actually run (aawv). 9 where the device has services to configure - fok5 and NZzD do parts of it inside 6, u--l does all of it after 7.

children.label: Prepare the devices
children.note: 1.1 to 1.3 on boxed hardware only (NZzD, u--l, fok5, 9yTg); 1.4 when the hardware will not enter setup mode (9yTg). 1.5 and 1.6 on the devices being replaced, in any order. 1.7 first on the new device, and 1.10 when the answer is wrong (mIjR, _CVz). 1.8 where a transfer will run long (aawv, CKwc). 1.9 where the route leans on a backup - CKwc and _CVz satisfy it by reading a timestamp instead of running one. 1.10 also serves goal 8: the same erase, at the other end of the task.

questions.question: What physical step does the page say must happen before continuing?
questions.why: The app explicitly instructs you to unplug the modem's power supply to properly reset the connection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically unplug the modem from the wall outlet as required by the setup instructions.

questions.question: Do you have all the required physical equipment and phone settings ready to begin setup?
questions.why: The screen lists specific physical items, like the gateway and cables, and phone settings, like Bluetooth and cellular data, needed to successfully complete the installation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically gather the required cables, modem, and eero devices or ensure your phone has Bluetooth and cellular data enabled.

questions.question: Have you located the included security screws?
questions.why: The app explicitly warns that using anything other than the provided short security screws could damage the device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically search the box to confirm the correct hardware has been found.

questions.question: Is your camera plugged in and powered on?
questions.why: The app requires you to confirm that the camera is physically connected to power and turned on before it can begin the pairing process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically plug the device into an outlet or visually verify that its power indicator has turned on.

questions.question: Did you wait for the router to finish its startup sequence before continuing?
questions.why: The screen explicitly advises waiting about a minute for the initialization process, and proceeding too early could cause the initial pairing to fail.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to physically check the router's indicator lights to confirm it has actually finished booting before moving forward.

questions.question: Have you removed the protective film from the device?
questions.why: Leaving the film in place can interfere with motion detection accuracy or cause it to permanently bond with the device surface.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent can click the confirmation button, but it cannot physically remove the film to ensure the hardware functions properly.

questions.question: Do you want to physically disable the microphone?
questions.why: Pressing the button with a crossed-out circle turns the device indicator red, providing visual confirmation that the microphone is shut off for privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the tactile familiarity of locating the hardware mute button and seeing its physical visual indicator.

questions.question: How do you orient the SIM card in the tray?
questions.why: Matching the diagonal slit on the SIM card to the tray's shape ensures the metal contacts face the correct way to be read by the device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically handle the SIM card to align its cut corner and insert it into the device's tray.

questions.question: Should you insert your SIM card now or skip this step?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to insert a SIM card or download an eSIM to connect to the mobile network, but skipping lets you maintain service on your old device during setup.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically proceed with the SIM setup, causing you to unexpectedly lose service on your active phone before you are fully ready to switch.

questions.question: Is your new phone on the initial setup screen or already on the home screen?
questions.why: Because the new phone is already displaying the home screen with standard apps instead of the initial 'Hello' screen, it must be factory reset before a direct data transfer can begin.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might fail to realize the device is in the wrong state and get stuck looking for a transfer prompt instead of performing the required factory reset.

children.label: Back up the old device
children.note: 1.9.1, then 1.9.2 where the account's sync settings matter. 1.9.3 to run one, or 1.9.4 on its own where a recent backup already exists (CKwc, _CVz). 1.9.5 only in pycZ.

questions.question: Should I tap 'Back Up Now' to start a fresh iCloud backup before the transfer?
questions.why: The screen displays the timestamp of the last successful backup, requiring a decision on whether that backup is recent enough or if a new one is needed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to judge if your most recent data is safely backed up before transferring it to the new device.

children.label: Erase a device
children.note: 1.10.1 then 1.10.2. 1.10.3 where a backup is offered first; 1.10.4 only where a cellular plan rides on the device being wiped (mIjR). 1.10.5 then 1.10.6 to go through with it - aawv is the only keeper that does. 1.10.7 is the other five, who reach the screen to show it and stop.

questions.question: How do you reset the device when the software settings are inaccessible?
questions.why: Closing the unresponsive software menu means you must rely on the device's physical buttons to perform a factory reset.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An AI agent cannot physically press the hardware buttons on the back of the device to initiate a hard reset.

questions.question: Should you update your iCloud backup before erasing the phone?
questions.why: The screen warns that erasing the device without updating the backup may result in the permanent loss of photos and other data not yet uploaded to iCloud.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically skip the backup to save time, potentially destroying your recent unsaved personal data.

questions.question: Am I absolutely sure I want to erase all data and reset this phone to factory settings?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns that proceeding will sign out of the Apple Account and permanently remove all apps, data, and Wallet items.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to verify that you don't have any unbacked-up personal data on the device before it is permanently wiped.

children.label: Start the setup
children.note: phone routes: 2.1, then 2.2 and 2.3 as the wizard asks - kB3r skips straight past both, _CVz ignores the language screen entirely. accessory routes: 2.4, then 2.5 to 2.8, all before any connection exists - which is why goal 3 follows this for them and precedes it for phones. 2.8 only where the device claims it needs a location (fok5, 9yTg).

questions.question: Are you setting this watch up for yourself or for a family member?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose between 'Set Up for Myself' and 'Set Up for a Family Member', which changes the entire configuration path.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent make this choice risks configuring the watch for the wrong user, preventing it from syncing correctly with your personal data.

questions.question: Do you need to enable any vision accessibility features before starting the setup?
questions.why: The screen offers options like magnification, font size adjustments, and TalkBack to customize the device for your visual needs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might skip accessibility settings that you rely on to comfortably read or navigate the screen.

questions.question: What address should you enter to access the router's admin panel?
questions.why: The inset image of the router's physical label displays 192.168.8.1 as the specific IP address required to reach the configuration page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the physical context of knowing where to find the router's default IP address on its hardware label for future troubleshooting.

questions.question: Which language do you want to use for the device?
questions.why: The welcome screen defaults to English, but tapping the globe icon allows you to select the language you are most comfortable reading.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means it might proceed with the default language instead of selecting your preferred native language.

questions.question: Which country or region should you select for your device?
questions.why: Choosing the correct country from the provided list ensures the device applies the appropriate regional settings, time zones, and network configurations.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might select an incorrect region, potentially restricting access to local apps, services, or correct time zones.

questions.question: Which Wi-Fi network should you select?
questions.why: The screen displays a list of available networks like "FFCSI-Corp" and "ATTWnbSMGs" alongside a "Skip" option, requiring you to identify your own network to enable data transfer and app downloads.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might not know your specific network credentials, potentially connecting to an insecure public network or skipping the connection entirely.

questions.question: What is the password for the selected Wi-Fi network?
questions.why: The screen prompts for the password of the chosen Wi-Fi network to connect the device to the internet.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user must expose their private home Wi-Fi password to the agent to complete the network connection.

questions.question: What rating and how many reviews does the store page show for this app?
questions.why: The app shows a 3.7-star rating across 36K reviews, which might contain important warnings about connectivity issues or privacy concerns.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to evaluate user feedback and potential red flags about the software that will control your smart home devices.

questions.question: Which app from the search results is the correct one to install?
questions.why: The top search result is an ad for an unrelated service, making it necessary to look past it and identify the official Ring app.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the correct, official companion app is being installed rather than a sponsored or potentially malicious alternative.

questions.question: Which room do you want to assign the device to?
questions.why: Grouping the device into a specific room helps it work and play together better with other devices in that same area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to organize your smart home layout according to where the device is actually physically placed.

questions.question: What name should you give this doorbell?
questions.why: The app requires you to select a location identifier like 'Front Door' or 'Back Door' to distinguish this device's notifications and feeds from others.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose a name that accurately reflects where you physically installed the device in your home.

questions.question: Should you provide a location for this device?
questions.why: Providing a location allows the device to give you relevant local weather and traffic information, but skipping it keeps your specific address private.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means you lose control over whether to share your physical address in exchange for localized weather and traffic updates.

children.label: Connect the two devices
children.note: 3.1 where the hardware has to be put into setup mode; 3.2 then 3.3 on the proximity routes; 3.4 on cable (kB3r). 3.5 then 3.6 on the accessory routes, and 3.5 leaves the app for the phone's own Wi-Fi settings and comes back through a banner. 3.7 always. 3.8 wherever any of it fails, which is four keepers.

questions.question: Should you turn on Bluetooth to discover the device, or skip this step?
questions.why: The app prompts you to enable Bluetooth to find and set up the new device, but offers a skip button if you want to bypass this method.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means you lose control over whether to enable your phone's Bluetooth for immediate pairing or skip the step entirely.

questions.question: Will you allow the app to access your phone's Bluetooth?
questions.why: The app requests Bluetooth access to establish a stable connection with the Ring device during setup.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent handle this means you lose control over which third-party apps are granted access to your phone's Bluetooth hardware.

questions.question: Is the camera's light flashing blue?
questions.why: The app requires you to confirm the physical camera is in setup mode by checking its LED status before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot see the physical device in your room to verify if the light is actually flashing.

questions.question: How do you want to pair the app with the device?
questions.why: The app offers the choice to either scan the QR code displayed on the Nest Hub or proceed without it using the manual setup code.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically point the phone's camera at the device's screen to scan the QR code.

questions.question: Which port should you plug the Ethernet cable into for the local network?
questions.why: The back of the router displays multiple ports including WAN and LAN, and selecting the correct LAN port is required to properly connect your local devices.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the hands-on knowledge of how your physical home network is wired and which specific ports remain available for future use.

questions.question: Should the app put your phone on the device's own temporary network?
questions.why: The app explains that this temporary network allows the phone to connect directly to the doorbell, and denying the prompt forces a manual connection process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses visibility into how the phone establishes its initial direct connection with the new hardware.

questions.question: Which network should I connect my phone to while the main network goes down?
questions.why: The Wi-Fi menu displays several alternative networks to choose from so the phone maintains internet access while the Eero temporarily disables the primary connection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing the ability to choose which specific backup network or mobile data plan you prefer to use during the temporary outage.

questions.question: Are you connecting to a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network as required by the device?
questions.why: The screen explicitly requires a 2.4 GHz network for setup, indicating this with a happy face icon while showing a sad face for 5 GHz.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to verify your home network's frequency, which could cause the setup to fail if the agent attempts to use an incompatible 5 GHz band.

questions.question: Why didn't the app prompt me for a Wi-Fi password after initially saying I could update it?
questions.why: Although the narrator claimed you could update the Wi-Fi password, the app connected automatically because the password was already saved to Google, as explained by the later on-screen text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually update your network password if the agent automatically relies on previously saved credentials.

questions.question: Did the app correctly identify the device you just scanned?
questions.why: Verifying the specific model shown on the screen ensures you are setting up the correct hardware before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the physical verification that the app recognized the exact device model you have in your hands.

questions.question: Which of the available devices is mine?
questions.why: Selecting the correct identifier from the available devices list ensures you connect to your specific Echo Dot rather than a neighbor's equipment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess the wrong device identifier if multiple are nearby, potentially attempting to pair with someone else's hardware.

questions.question: How do you want to proceed after the initial connection attempt fails?
questions.why: The screen displays a connection error with specific troubleshooting instructions and options to either get help or try again.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to immediately retry the connection or investigate their phone's privacy settings first.

questions.question: Can you reconfigure the Wi-Fi network directly from this settings menu?
questions.why: The network option displays a crossed-out Wi-Fi icon and 'Not connected,' but it is actually grayed out and unresponsive, meaning you must find an alternative way to reset the connection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate tactile realization that the menu option is unresponsive, which prompts the necessary pivot to a factory reset.

children.label: Sign in and authorize
children.note: 4.1 first - DT4C refuses an account outright and 9yTg's account creation is edited out. then 4.2 or 4.3 by route: phone transfers authorize with the old device's passcode, everything else with account credentials. 4.4 and 4.5 where the account pushes verification to another device. 4.6 only in c_gv, 4.7 only in pycZ.

questions.question: Do you want fingerprint or face sign-in for this app?
questions.why: The app offers to enable Touch ID for faster future access to your account, which changes your login security preferences.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent deciding whether to enable biometric authentication removes your control over how your personal device security features are used.

questions.question: Do you want to sign in to your Google account now, create a new one, or skip this step?
questions.why: The screen provides options to authenticate with an existing email or phone, create a new account, or skip the Google sign-in process entirely.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over whether their personal Google account is linked to the device during the initial setup or if this step is deferred.

questions.question: Are you sure you want to skip setting up an Apple ID?
questions.why: The screen warns that skipping this step prevents access to essential services like the App Store, iCloud, and Apple Pay.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to have their core Apple services and cloud backups automatically configured during the initial setup.

questions.question: What name and date of birth should you provide?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that the date of birth determines which services are set up on the iPhone, affecting age-appropriate features.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure their actual identity and age are used to correctly configure age-restricted services and account recovery details.

questions.question: What is the password for my Apple ID?
questions.why: The screen prompts for your Apple ID password to authenticate the account and proceed with the device setup.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing your highly sensitive Apple ID password with a third-party agent.

questions.question: Which passcode do you need to enter to authorize the data transfer?
questions.why: The screen explicitly states that your account is protected by the passcode of your other iPhone and requires it to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires sharing your existing device's highly sensitive unlock passcode with a third-party agent.

questions.question: Do you recognize this sign-in attempt and location to allow it?
questions.why: The prompt displays a location for the sign-in attempt, which you must verify is legitimate before granting access and receiving the verification code.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing the ability to personally verify if the location shown on the map matches your actual whereabouts for this sign-in attempt.

questions.question: Do you notice the discrepancy in the sign-in location between the lock screen notification and the map pop-up?
questions.why: Spotting that the notification says Monrovia while the map shows Los Angeles is important for verifying if the sign-in attempt is genuinely yours before approving it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally evaluate these conflicting location details to determine if the authentication request is actually safe to approve.

questions.question: How will you provide the 6-digit verification code sent to your phone?
questions.why: The screen requires a 6-digit verification code sent via text message to confirm your identity before completing the Google account sign-in.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent cannot proceed without real-time access to the personal text messages sent to your phone.

questions.question: Are you aware the setup flow switched from creating a new account to verifying an existing one?
questions.why: Selecting 'Create a Free Apple Account' contradicts the subsequent prompt for a verification code sent to other trusted devices, indicating a mismatch in the setup flow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly proceed with an existing account instead of creating a new one as requested, compromising your intended account separation.

children.label: Choose what to transfer
children.note: 5.1 picks the source, and two keepers pick nothing (uSN0, DT4C's first pass) - the rest of this goal is a no-op for them. 5.2 where more than one route exists; 5.3 where a stored backup or a plan has to be named. 5.4 before starting. 5.5 wherever a route is looked at and not taken. then 5.6 and 5.7. 5.6 is the last point at which anything is reversible.

questions.question: Do you want to transfer your phone number now or set it up later?
questions.why: The screen warns that transferring your phone number will immediately disable it on your old device, making the timing of this switch important.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide might result in your old phone unexpectedly losing cellular service before you are fully ready to switch to the new device.

questions.question: Which method should you choose to bring your data over?
questions.why: The screen provides multiple options for migrating your information, such as copying wirelessly from an old phone, restoring from a cloud backup, or choosing not to copy anything.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might select a transfer method that does not align with where your most recent or complete backup is actually stored.

questions.question: Which device backup do you want to restore?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple previous device backups with timestamps, requiring you to identify the correct source device to ensure your current data transfers over.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select an outdated backup or skip the restore entirely, leaving your new phone without your expected apps and personal data.

questions.question: Does the page say the selected number's transfer is not supported?
questions.why: The screen lists your available phone numbers for transfer but warns that the transfer is not supported for the selected number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to proceed with the unsupported transfer attempt or skip it to contact your carrier directly.

questions.question: Which specific data categories do you want to restore from your backup?
questions.why: The screen lists categories like apps, contacts, and messages to restore, which directly impacts how much storage is used on the new device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means losing the ability to filter out unwanted apps or data from the backup, potentially cluttering the new device.

questions.question: Does the restore total drop by the size of the apps that were unselected?
questions.why: The screen showed the total restore size updating to reflect the 0.2 GB saved by excluding those specific apps.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate feedback of seeing exactly how much storage space is saved by their specific selections.

questions.question: Are you ready to start transferring data from your previous iPhone?
questions.why: The screen estimates the transfer will take 5 to 10 minutes, so you must decide if you have time to wait now or prefer other options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to postpone the transfer if you need your phone immediately or prefer setting it up as a new device.

children.label: Work through the setup screens
children.note: 6.1 to 6.10 in whatever order the vendor's wizard asks - no keeper reorders them and none sees all of them. 6.1 and 6.2 are what split the corpus: c_gv accepts through both, DT4C declines through both, uSN0 does one of each. 6.8 and 6.9 only on the eSIM route. 6.11 ends it. c_gv and DT4C run this whole goal twice on the same phone, and Apple Pay and Siri get asked in both passes.

questions.question: Do you want to use the pre-filled first and last name for your profile?
questions.why: The screen states that Alexa will use this name to get to know you better, which determines how the assistant will address you.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose a specific nickname or preferred name for the voice assistant to use.

questions.question: Should you grant the app access to your contacts and allow notifications?
questions.why: The screen explains that uploading contacts helps you connect with family and friends, but granting these system-level permissions directly impacts your data privacy and device interruptions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically allow or deny these permissions, bypassing your personal boundaries regarding data privacy and notification preferences.

children.label: Set the device locks
children.note: 6.1.1 or 6.1.5 - a lock or a refusal. 6.1.2 only where the passcode is weak enough to be challenged. 6.1.3 then 6.1.4 where a biometric is enrolled. DT4C does both: defers the biometric and still has to set a passcode.

questions.question: Do you want to set up the face or fingerprint unlock now, or add it later?
questions.why: This determines whether you configure biometric authentication immediately to unlock the phone and make purchases, or skip it to save time during the initial setup.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically scan your face, so delegating this step means you lose the ability to configure biometric security during the initial setup.

questions.question: Should you set up security questions for admin password recovery?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to select and answer two personal questions to ensure you can recover your admin password if you forget it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might skip the setup or choose security answers you do not know, potentially leaving you unable to recover a forgotten password.

questions.question: Does this second entry exactly match the six-digit passcode I just created?
questions.why: The screen requires you to re-enter the six digits to confirm your new passcode and prevent accidental lockouts from typos.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means sharing your primary device unlock code with an agent, compromising your personal security.

questions.question: Do you want to use the easily guessed passcode anyway or change it to a stronger one?
questions.why: The screen warns that this passcode protects access to your iPhone and iCloud data, meaning a weak passcode lowers your overall security.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might choose to use the weak passcode to speed up the setup process, leaving your personal device and data vulnerable.

questions.question: Did your first Face ID scan finish?
questions.why: The screen confirms the first scan is complete, which is necessary before you can proceed to the second scan to finish biometric setup.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the physical agency to position their own face and ensure their biometric security is configured accurately.

questions.question: Should you rename this fingerprint or accept the default?
questions.why: The screen confirms the fingerprint is enrolled and offers the option to rename it from the default "Fingerprint ID 1" or just tap "OK" to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to give the fingerprint a memorable custom name instead of the generic default.

children.label: Answer the consent screens
children.note: 6.2.1 always. the rest as the vendor asks: Google runs 6.2.2, 6.2.4 and 6.2.5 as one block (kB3r, fok5), Apple asks 6.2.3 twice on the same phone (DT4C). 6.2.6 only in NZzD, where it is pre-checked and never discussed.

questions.question: Do you agree to the terms and conditions?
questions.why: The screen presents the mandatory legal agreements required to use the iOS device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read and understand the specific legal terms and privacy policies you are consenting to.

questions.question: Do you accept the Google Terms of Service and the binding arbitration agreement?
questions.why: Proceeding requires agreeing to Google's legal terms, which includes a binding individual arbitration agreement that affects how disputes are resolved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the specific legal terms and privacy policies you are being bound to before proceeding.

questions.question: Do you want to keep Google Drive backup enabled for this account?
questions.why: Turning off the backup toggle triggers a warning that the existing device backup for your account will be permanently deleted from Google Drive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means an agent might permanently delete your existing cloud backup or sync your data to the wrong account without your consent.

questions.question: Do you want to share your usage data with the maker?
questions.why: This determines whether your device sends background usage data to help Apple improve its products and services.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to enforce your personal privacy boundaries regarding background data collection.

questions.question: Do you want to set up a voice profile now?
questions.why: Creating a voice profile allows Alexa to recognize you and personalize responses, but requires agreeing to store your voice data in the cloud.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot speak with your actual voice to train the profile, meaning this specific personalization step must be skipped or done manually by you.

questions.question: Do you want to share your Siri audio recordings with Apple?
questions.why: This choice determines whether Apple is allowed to store your audio interactions with Siri, which directly impacts your privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your privacy preferences regarding whether your voice recordings are stored and shared with Apple.

questions.question: Do you want to enable Amazon Sidewalk to share your device's approximate location?
questions.why: This setting applies to all your linked Echo and Ring devices and shares your approximate location to help neighbors find connected items, which directly impacts your privacy.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically opt you into this community network, sharing your location data and bandwidth without your explicit consent.

questions.question: Should you enable location services?
questions.why: This determines whether apps like Maps and Find My are allowed to gather and use data about your approximate location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent make this choice means you lose direct control over your personal privacy and location tracking preferences.

questions.question: Do you want to set up the optional extras now, or get a reminder to finish later?
questions.why: The screen offers the choice to either complete the setup for optional features immediately or postpone them with a reminder.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether they want to invest time right now to configure optional features or defer them until later.

questions.question: Do you want to add the suggested credit card to Apple Pay now or skip it?
