questions.question: Is the dispute actually listed in your open cases?
questions.why: Although the submission seemed complete, the Resolution Center shows zero open cases, indicating the claim may not have been successfully recorded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent assumes the dispute was filed without verifying the open cases list, you might lose your money because the claim was never actually processed.

questions.question: How do you want to proceed now that the message to the seller has been sent?
questions.why: The screen confirms the message was sent to Wish.com and notes that PayPal can help if the issue isn't resolved directly, prompting a choice on what to do next.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to wait for the seller's response or immediately review the transaction details.

questions.question: Are these the correct details for the dispute case you are reviewing?
questions.why: Expanding the case details allows you to verify the disputed amount, seller information, and shipping address to ensure the correct claim is being handled.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the correct transaction and seller details were accurately recorded for your dispute.

questions.question: Which closed dispute case do you want to review?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple closed cases with different Case IDs and amounts, so you must select the correct one to view its specific details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the history and resolution details of a specific past dispute.

questions.question: What is the outcome and timeline of your dispute?
questions.why: Reviewing the case timeline confirms that the dispute was closed in your favor and a refund was issued.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the direct reassurance of seeing the exact resolution timeline and the confirmation of your refund.

questions.question: How do you know who is reviewing the dispute after the seller responds?
questions.why: The dashboard updates to show 'In corso di revisione da parte di PayPal', indicating that PayPal has taken over the review process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the reassurance of seeing exactly where their dispute stands and who is currently responsible for the next step.

questions.question: How do you escalate the unresolved dispute to PayPal?
questions.why: The screen displays a warning that the case will automatically close by a specific date unless you click 'Inoltra a PayPal' to convert it into a formal claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over the timing of the escalation, as you might prefer to wait for the merchant's response before officially involving PayPal.

questions.question: Should you change the case type to better fit the issue you are facing?
questions.why: The screen offers alternative options like reporting a lost card or an unauthorized subscription to ensure the dispute is categorized correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to verify if a different dispute category better matches the specific details of your fraudulent transaction.

children.label: Appeal the outcome
children.note: 8.6.1 then 8.6.2; the evidence and the submission reuse 6.5, 6.6 and 7.1

questions.question: What are the details of the case you need to appeal?
questions.why: The email displays the specific case ID and outcome needed to identify which transaction to address in PayPal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to review the specific context and case number of the dispute before taking action in your account.

questions.question: What is your reason for filing this appeal?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify whether you will provide tracking information or proof of a previous refund to support your appeal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might select an appeal reason you cannot actually provide proof for, which could cause your claim to be denied.

questions.question: How did you issue the refund?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify whether the refund was issued through PayPal or another method to ensure the dispute is processed correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately report your specific refund method, which could lead to the dispute being mishandled if the agent guesses incorrectly.

questions.question: Am I sure I want to permanently close this case, knowing I cannot reopen it?
questions.why: The warning modal explicitly states that once the case is closed, you cannot report another issue on this transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether they are truly ready to permanently forfeit their right to dispute this specific transaction.

questions.question: Are there any open cases in your queue that you can close?
questions.why: The Resolution Centre displays '0 Open cases' and states there are no cases in your queue, indicating no active disputes are currently available to manage or close.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally verify the status of your open cases and manually close any resolved disputes.

questions.question: How do you report another issue for a transaction that already has a closed case?
questions.why: The screen shows the initial case is already closed with a refund issued, so you must find the specific option to open a new dispute for the same transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to ensure all separate issues with a multi-item transaction are fully addressed and refunded.

children.note: 9.1 or 9.2 before the next send; 9.3 where the platform sells refund insurance

dmv.task: renew a driver's license or vehicle registration on a state DMV portal: verify identity and eligibility, work through the renewal form, pay the fee; complete when the renewal-submitted confirmation — receipt or temporary document — is on screen. Surface pinned: a state DMV web portal, not an in-office visit vlog. Variants: address change (seeded variant), first-time license applications, REAL ID upgrades, and driving-test booking do not belong.

tree.label: Renew a DMV credential online
tree.note: 1 and 2 in the order the venue dictates - account venues meet 3 first and reach the service from the dashboard (DeKE, w74r, _xgB); the rest run 1, then 2, then 3. 2.4 and 2.5 fire before or mid-task as the requirements demand (w74r, YWFI). then 4, with 5 interleaved wherever the wizard asks. 6 only on the carrier systems, then 7 once the approval lands (-eBX, F_2L), then 8. no keeper re-enters an earlier goal by choice - the one reach-back is 7 into 5.8 when a missing email blocks payment (DeKE).

children.label: Find the renewal service
children.note: 1.1 or 1.2 to arrive, then one of 1.3, 1.4, or 1.5 as the venue offers. 1.5 comes after 3 on account venues - the dashboard is behind the login.

questions.question: Does the site handling this renewal identify itself as the official one for your jurisdiction, rather than a general portal or a lookalike?
questions.why: The address bar shows navigation to a specific county tax collector site (pbctax.com) rather than a general state DMV portal, which dictates where the renewal is processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to ensure the agent uses their specific local county portal rather than a general state website.

questions.question: Does the result about to be opened carry the official government domain, rather than a third-party or phishing copy of the agency's portal?
questions.why: Verifying that the search result URL contains the official government domain ensures you are entering the legitimate LTMS portal rather than a third-party or phishing site.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally inspect the URL and confirm that your sensitive identity information will be submitted to the authentic government agency.

children.label: Browse the menus to the service
Pick the service from the shortcuts

questions.question: Does the dashboard's renewal reminder name the credential you actually intend to renew?
questions.why: The dashboard displays a specific vehicle renewal reminder alongside multiple menu options like 'LICENSING' and 'VEHICLE'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the visibility of their dashboard reminders and the ability to personally confirm exactly which vehicle is currently due for renewal.

questions.question: Which registration period do you want to renew?
questions.why: The dashboard lists multiple periods, such as '30-Apr-2019' and '30-Apr-2018', and requires you to select one to proceed with the vehicle renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the correct registration year and associated balance is chosen for your account.

children.label: Confirm eligibility and requirements
children.note: 2.1 where a notice exists - the pages after it repeat what the notice already said (hI3L, 7b3U). 2.2, 2.3, and 2.6 in the order the pages present them. 2.4 and 2.5 whenever the requirements reach into the physical world, mid-task included (w74r, YWFI). then 2.7, with 2.8 wherever a terms gate blocks the path.

questions.question: Do you want to schedule an in-person appointment if the online system cannot process your renewal?
questions.why: The page displayed a banner stating online processing was unavailable due to the expiration date and provided a link to make an appointment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to abandon the online task or proceed with scheduling an in-office visit.

questions.question: Does the renewal notice say a smog check is required before you can renew?
questions.why: The renewal notice explicitly states that a smog certification is required and provides the website URL and identification number needed to renew online.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally verify prerequisites like a required smog check before initiating the online renewal.

questions.question: What details does the renewal notice show, before 'Process Renewal' starts the renewal itself?
questions.why: The IRP Menu displays multiple similar options like 'Process Renewal' and 'Print Renewal Notice', making it important to know which specific link actually initiates the information-gathering step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to personally review the printed renewal notice and verify your vehicle details before the renewal is processed.

questions.question: Do the conditions for a first provisional license apply to my situation?
questions.why: The screen lists specific criteria for a first provisional license, such as never having applied before or applying before March 1973, which dictates whether you must complete this section or skip it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify your driving history against the portal's specific criteria to ensure the correct application path is chosen.

questions.question: Do any of these conditions apply to me that would prevent me from renewing online?
questions.why: The screen lists specific conditions, such as needing a road test or an updated medical report, that mandate an in-person visit instead of an online renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might incorrectly assume you are eligible to renew online without knowing your personal medical status or testing requirements.

questions.question: Do any special renewal conditions, like being 70 or over, apply to you?
questions.why: The screen lists alternative renewal links for specific situations like being 70 or over, driving a bus, or having a medical license, which dictate whether you can use the standard process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the opportunity to personally verify if your specific age, vehicle type, or medical status requires a specialized renewal path.

questions.question: Which remote renewal method do you want to use?
questions.why: The notice provides three different options for renewing—by phone, mail, or online—each with specific requirements like a 14-digit authorization number or a check.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate the requirements for each method and select the one most convenient for your situation.

questions.question: Did you provide the required vision test results to continue with the renewal?
questions.why: The portal explicitly states that an eye test from an approved provider is required, but the session ends without resolving this step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to successfully complete the renewal because a mandatory eligibility requirement was ignored.

children.label: Read the fee and time quotes

questions.question: What does the page say the renewal costs and how long does the new licence last?
questions.why: The screen displays the £14 fee and the 10-year renewal requirement, which are essential facts to confirm before starting the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the exact cost and eligibility rules before committing to the renewal process.

questions.question: How long will it take to receive your new license?
questions.why: The screen states the license should arrive within a week, which sets expectations for when you will receive the physical document.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct reassurance of knowing exactly when to expect your new physical license in the mail.

questions.question: Do you have the items the site says you need before it will start?
questions.why: The 'Before you start' screen explicitly states that these items are required to create an account and proceed with the renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally confirm that you have the required email access and identification documents ready before initiating the state portal process.

questions.question: Do you want to accept or reject analytics cookies before continuing?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose your privacy preferences regarding analytics cookies before you can proceed with the renewal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to control your privacy preferences regarding how the DMV tracks your usage of the service.

questions.question: Do you agree to the site's terms of use so the application can open?
questions.why: The screen displays a mandatory terms of use modal that must be accepted to access the renewal system.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the opportunity to personally review and consent to the legal terms governing your use of the DMV portal.

children.label: Pass the identity gate
children.note: one route per venue: 3.1 then 3.2 on account systems; 3.3 then 3.4 on record-search systems; 3.5 on knowledge-field systems; 3.6 where the authorization number comes off a mailed letter. iV8P switches mid-flow from 3.5 to 3.1. two keepers never get past this goal (7t4w, iV8P).

children.label: Decide to log in or register

questions.question: Do you already have an account on this site, so registering again would create a duplicate profile?
questions.why: The portal homepage requires you to choose between 'REGISTER NOW' and 'LOG IN' to access the system based on your prior account status.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent must know whether you already have an established account with the DMV to avoid creating duplicate profiles.

questions.why: The login screen requires either an email address or an LTO client number along with a password to access the renewal portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user must share their private login credentials with the agent, compromising their account security.

questions.question: How do you want to search for your vehicle registration?
questions.why: The portal requires you to select a search type from a dropdown menu, which dictates whether you need to provide a PIN or other identifying details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select a search method that requires specific numbers or documents you do not have readily available.

questions.question: Is this vehicle registered under a personal number or a commercial registration number?
questions.why: The dropdown menu requires you to specify whether the vehicle is registered to a company or an individual to locate the correct records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the guarantee that the vehicle is being renewed under the correct legal ownership classification.

questions.question: What are your vehicle's plate number, category, and code?
questions.why: The 'Plate details' search form requires your exact plate number, category, and code to locate your specific vehicle registration record.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the correct vehicle plate details are entered to pull up your registration.

questions.question: What identity details does the guest renewal require you to provide?

questions.question: Does the user read the license and authorization numbers off their own mailed notice rather than passing them to the agent?
questions.why: The screen requires a Driver's License Number and Authorization Number from your physical documents or renewal letter to proceed, and provides a phone number to call if the PIN is missing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would need access to your physical ID card and private renewal letter to find the required numbers, or they would have to call the DMV on your behalf.

questions.question: Does the page warn that a processing fee will be added on top of the base fee?
questions.why: The screen confirms your approval for Safe Driver Renewal and discloses the $30.00 base fee alongside a warning about an additional payment processor fee.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify your approval status and acknowledge the upcoming processing fees before committing to the payment phase.

children.label: Verify and complete the record
children.note: 4.1 where the account lists vehicles; 4.2 on the fleet systems. then 4.3 against the notice, the insurance, and the inspection. 4.4 to 4.7 as the venue's record demands - document validation on LTMS, insurance on OkCARS, mileage on the carrier systems. 4.8 where the wizard asks for addresses; 4.9 only on licence renewals, where the form asks about the person rather than a vehicle.

questions.question: Did the search return your correct vehicle, and is it selected for renewal?
questions.why: The screen displays registrations matching your search criteria, so you must verify the correct vehicle is checked before moving on to select the renewal type.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally confirm that the correct vehicle from your profile or search was selected for renewal.

questions.question: Which of your listed vehicles do you want to renew, or is your vehicle missing from the list?
questions.why: The screen requires you to select a specific registered vehicle to renew or indicate if it is not listed, which determines if you can proceed online.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the correct vehicle is selected for renewal or to learn that unlisted vehicles require an in-person visit.

questions.question: Are the vehicle details the page shows for this unit still correct?
questions.why: The portal provides an update button to review and modify specific vehicle details like the unit number and unladen weight before finalizing the renewal.

questions.question: How many power units are you renewing this year?

questions.question: Is the pre-filled Certificate of Coverage number correct?
questions.why: Verifying the automatically populated COC number ensures that the correct emission test results are linked to your renewal application.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to provide their actual insurance policy number, risking a rejected renewal due to unverified coverage.

questions.question: What were your actual miles traveled in each jurisdiction during the previous registration year?
questions.why: The screen requires you to enter the actual miles traveled in each jurisdiction to complete this section of the renewal form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might enter incorrect mileage data, potentially leading to inaccurate registration fees or compliance issues.

questions.question: What information must you add to resolve the incomplete registration alert?
questions.why: The screen displays a warning that the registration is incomplete because reported distances or vehicles must be added to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to verify the exact distance or vehicle details being submitted for your registration.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally verify that your specific fleet mileage data was entered and calculated correctly for each state.

questions.question: Does the form offer a military exemption to claim?

download.task: find and download a specific file (a government form PDF, a bank statement, a schedule/timetable PDF, a paper, a receipt/invoice): locate the artifact on the site, trigger the download, and verify the file actually arrived (the downloads bar or downloads folder shows the right file); complete when the downloaded file is visible in the downloads UI or opened. Surface pinned: any site's download flow plus the browser's download UI. Variants: piracy/torrent content, download-manager-software ads, and "how to download YouTube videos" (rights-violating rips) do not belong.

tree.label: Find, download, and verify a specific file

ebay.task: bid on an eBay auction as a buyer: find an auction listing, review item condition, seller rating, and shipping, place a bid by setting a maximum bid, confirm the bid, and see the resulting bid status; complete when the bid-confirmed state ("You're the highest bidder" or "You've been outbid") is on screen. Surface pinned: the eBay website or app. Variants: selling or listing items, dropshipping/reselling content, "Buy It Now" only purchases (that is ordinary shopping), and sniping-tool promotions do not belong.

tree.label: Win an eBay auction
tree.note: 1 where the account demands it - most keepers arrive signed in. 2 unless the listing is already at hand - ten keepers open on the target. then 3, then 4; T5mb runs 3.5 before anything else. 5 stages the bid - 5.2 replaces the bid box for the three accounts with no payment on file, and none of them ever bids. 6 owns the clock: snipers hold inside it, immediate bidders fall straight through to 6.6 (08WT, s_CE, B7Zu, fAtx). 7 whenever the outbid notice lands - it can interrupt 6 or follow it. 8 when the clock resolves; a loss ends there. 9 after a win, and 9.4 loops the whole task back to 2 - six times in Zkom. fx1m runs 5 and 6 across four windows at once.

email.task: compose and send an email in a mail client (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo Mail, Apple Mail): open compose, address the recipient, write the subject and body, optionally attach a file, send it, and verify it in Sent; complete when the message shows as sent. Surface pinned: the mail client's compose-and-send flow — not inbox-organizing tours, not newsletter/marketing tools, not email-etiquette advice videos.

tree.label: Send an email
tree.note: 1 when the client is not already open and signed in - most keepers start authenticated and skip most of it. then 2: a new message, or a reply or forward entered from 8.1 (DFXu, ycKB, 6rzA, 0D7H, zCsj), which decides how much of 3 is left to do. 3 and 4 in either order - HnFK writes the subject and body before the recipient. 5 where the message carries a file; 5.4 only when the client refuses the file, and it returns into 5.2 or 5.5 once the file is ready (UehN never gets back). then 6, one of 6.2 to 6.5; 6.6 and 6.7 where the client interrupts. then 7 - in this corpus that's where the task actually completes, and 7 is skipped by seven keepers. 8 at any point.

children.label: Get into the mailbox

flights.task: book a flight online (Google Flights, airline websites and apps, Expedia, Kayak): search a route and dates, compare fares and times, pick an outbound and return, enter passenger details, and reach the payment or confirmation step; complete when a booking confirmation or itinerary summary with the fare total is on screen. Surface pinned: a flight-booking site or airline app — not an airport kiosk, not a travel vlog, not a points/miles explainer without a live booking session. Variants: checking in for a flight (see checkin), researching and comparing without booking (see itinerary), and hotel or car add-ons after the flight is booked do not belong.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to manually include or exclude specific airlines based on your personal past experiences or loyalty memberships.

questions.question: Should you rely on the default ranking for price and convenience, or adjust the sorting options to find the best flight?
questions.why: The screen defaults to ranking flights by a mix of price and convenience, requiring a choice on whether to trust this order or explore other sorting methods.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might just select the top recommended flight, missing your personal preferences for balancing cost, layovers, and specific airlines.

questions.question: Do you want to sort the flight results by carbon emissions?
questions.why: The 'Sort by' dropdown includes an 'Emissions' option, allowing you to prioritize greener flights over the cheapest or fastest routes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to align your travel choices with your environmental values if the agent only optimizes for price or duration.

questions.question: Do the outbound and return legs use different airports in the same city?
questions.why: The screen displays a direct round trip for C$ 340 involving different Toronto-area airports, requiring you to confirm if these specific logistics fit your travel plans.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally weigh the convenience of the specific flight times and airport locations against the ticket price.

questions.question: Does this itinerary require a self-transfer or separate tickets that leave you unprotected if a flight is delayed?
questions.why: Aggregators often bundle separate one-way tickets on different airlines to save money, meaning you must collect and re-check baggage yourself and are not protected if the first leg is delayed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might book a risky 'hacker fare' to save a few dollars, leaving you stranded and forced to buy a new same-day ticket out of pocket if you miss the connection.

questions.question: Which flight should you select from the search results?
questions.why: You need to evaluate the different departure times and prices, such as the ₹4,049 morning flight versus the ₹4,200 evening flight, to find the best option.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally balance your schedule preferences against the specific price differences shown.

questions.question: Which returning flight should you select?
questions.why: The screen showed multiple return options from Boracay to Manila, such as an earlier flight for PHP 3,954.68 and a later, cheaper one for PHP 2,900.76.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means losing the ability to balance your preferred departure time against the cost savings of a cheaper ticket.

children.label: Choose where to book
children.note: 4.1 with 4.2 against it, then 4.3. 4.4 when the first provider disappoints, looping back through 4.1 (DTJW). 4.5 right after landing - the two keepers who run it are the two that catch the handoff changing the numbers. only the metasearch keepers run this goal at all; airline-direct and single-OTA paths never see it.

questions.question: Which booking provider should you select to purchase this ticket?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple booking agencies with varying prices alongside a warning to check for extra fees and terms.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to balance the lowest fare against the reliability and specific terms of the third-party booking agency.

questions.question: Did the handoff land on the seller that was chosen?
questions.why: The interstitial screen requires clicking 'Continue to booking' to successfully redirect from the search aggregator to the final booking site.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness of being handed off to a third-party booking site to complete your reservation.

questions.question: Does the price on the booking site match the aggregator's quote?
questions.why: This matters because the initial Skyscanner screen listed the total as 126 €, but the subsequent Mytrip redirect screen displayed €125.99.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might ignore price discrepancies during redirects, preventing you from catching potential bait-and-switch pricing tactics from third-party sites.

questions.question: Does the itinerary on the booking site match the flight picked on the aggregator?
questions.why: Verifying the Mumbai to New Delhi flight times and the 15 kg baggage allowance ensures you selected the right itinerary before providing personal information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to catch a mistake in the departure time or baggage limit before committing your personal details to the reservation.

children.label: Choose the fare tier
children.note: 5.1 then 5.2 - per leg where the site asks per leg (MasT, lc1q, Q4Km, 15Vk), once for the whole trip where it does not (d2oz, WZ5A, CtaK). 5.3 when a cheap pick triggers a defense modal (DTJW). WZ5A re-enters here from the bags step through the stepper's Change fare, and never comes back.

questions.question: Do the benefits promised on the initial fare card match what is shown in the fare comparison table?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to catch conflicting fare terms and avoid paying extra for a premium tier that fails to deliver the promised benefits.

questions.question: Is the fare bundle a better deal than buying a checked bag separately?

questions.question: Which fare tier offers the right balance of price and flexibility for your trip?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple fare options like Economy Semi Flex for 687 USD with change fees versus Eco Flex with free changes, requiring a choice based on your need for flexibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether saving money upfront is worth the risk of paying higher change or cancellation fees later.

questions.question: Do you want to pay to upgrade the fare you already chose, or keep it?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns that the Saver ticket has no flexibility and charges a 30 € fee for later changes, offering a Standard upgrade for 49.17 €.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically buy the upgrade to avoid penalty risks, spending extra money you would have preferred to save.

children.label: Enter the passenger details
children.note: 6.1 or 6.2 per passenger; 6.3 and 6.4 as the form asks. then 6.5. 6.6 when the submit fails - twice triggered on purpose, once by silent state loss.

questions.question: Does the selected saved profile match the traveler being booked?
questions.why: Choosing the correct pre-existing profile ensures the booking details match the traveler's ID exactly without manual entry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify exactly which of their saved contacts is traveling on this ticket.

questions.question: Do the name, date of birth, and gender entered match the passenger's passport exactly?
questions.why: The screen requires your exact name, date of birth, and gender to issue a valid ticket, while offering optional fields for frequent flyer numbers and special requests.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure their name matches their passport exactly and the opportunity to attach their frequent flyer account to the booking.

questions.question: Does your passport have as long left on it as the page requires?
questions.why: The screen displays a warning to ensure the passenger's travel document has at least a 4-month validity, which is a strict requirement for this specific trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to realize their passport might expire too soon, which would result in being denied boarding despite having a valid ticket.

questions.question: Do you want to add a frequent flyer number?
questions.why: The form includes optional fields for a frequent flyer program and number, which allows you to earn miles for the trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent skips this step without asking, you miss out on earning miles or loyalty points for your flight.

questions.question: Do you need to add your GST details for this booking?

questions.question: Who do you want to set as the main contact for booking confirmations and updates?

questions.question: Do you want to opt into SMS and email notifications before continuing?

questions.question: Does every filled field match the traveler's actual details?
questions.why: Verifying your contact information before clicking 'Continue' ensures the 3,025,311 NGN trip is booked under the correct passenger details.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to double-check your personal information for typos before the agent advances to the seat selection step.

questions.question: Why did your form submission fail, and which passenger profile must you select to proceed?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the correct saved passenger profile is chosen when resolving the form submission error.

children.label: Add or decline the extras
children.note: 7.1 to 7.5 in whatever order the site's stepper runs them; every child is a priced offer and most keepers decline most of them. 7.3 fires when 7.2 says no. three offers arrive pre-set - bags pre-added (Q4Km), insurance pre-selected (MasT), paid seats pre-assigned (Q4Km) - so declining means finding the removal control first.

children.label: Choose the seats
children.note: 7.1.1 then 7.1.2 per flight; 7.1.3 instead where the seat is skipped or arrives pre-assigned.

questions.question: Do you want to pay an extra fee to select a specific seat, or skip seat selection to save money?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether securing a specific seat is worth paying the additional fee.

questions.question: On the visual seat map, is the assigned seat a middle seat or located directly next to the lavatories?
questions.why: Seat numbers alone (like 28E) don't always clearly convey if it's a middle seat or in an undesirable location, which is immediately obvious to a sighted user looking at the graphical layout.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to avoid an uncomfortable middle seat or a noisy spot by the bathrooms because the agent only verified the seat number and price.

questions.question: Are there actually adjacent seats available for your group to sit together, or is the cabin mostly full?
questions.why: Even if you are willing to pay extra for seat selection, the seat map might reveal that no two seats are together, which is a dealbreaker for families traveling with children.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to abandon the booking for this specific flight before paying, avoiding a situation where your young child is forced to sit alone.

questions.question: Did the seat map actually assign you the seat you clicked, or did it throw an error saying the seat is no longer available?
questions.why: Seat maps can display stale inventory, and the seat you select might have been taken by another user moments before.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might proceed thinking they secured a specific seat, when the system actually rejected the selection and left it unassigned.

questions.question: Do you want to confirm your choice to skip seat selection?
questions.why: The site displays a warning modal asking if you want to proceed because seats were not selected for all passengers.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether securing specific seats is important enough to go back and select them.

questions.question: Do you need to add checked baggage for an additional fee?
questions.why: Adding a 20 kg checked bag significantly increases the fare, as shown when the total jumped from 118 € to 218.10 €.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether your specific packing needs justify paying a steep baggage fee.

questions.question: Is the baggage summary correct, and is the current booking total acceptable before you move on to seat selection?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally ensure your specific luggage needs are accurately reflected in the price before proceeding.

questions.question: Are you sure you want to decline checked baggage now and risk paying higher fees at the airport?
questions.why: The warning modal explicitly shows that buying a 15 kg baggage allowance at the airport costs ¥4,600, compared to just ¥1,780 if purchased now.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to weigh your actual packing needs against the financial risk of paying a premium at the airport.

questions.question: Do you want to add Price Drop Protection to your search?
questions.why: The search screen includes an option to 'Add Price Drop Protection', where the platform will pay the difference if the price drops after booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to secure financial protection against future price drops before initiating the search.

questions.question: Do you want to add the flight protection plan before completing the booking?
questions.why: The screen requires you to explicitly choose whether to add or decline the $35.28 flight protection plan before the system will process the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might make the wrong choice about purchasing travel insurance or fail the form submission entirely by skipping the required selection.

questions.question: Should you add any optional extras like Wi-Fi or a stopover package to your booking?
questions.why: The booking flow presents optional add-ons like in-flight Wi-Fi for 6,960 NGN or an Addis stopover package for 153,120 NGN that will increase your total fare.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically skip these extras to minimize costs, depriving you of amenities you might prefer for a more comfortable journey.

questions.question: Do you want to go back to purchase add-ons now to save money, or proceed without them?
questions.why: The modal warns that add-on prices will increase if you wait to add them after booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to decide whether to secure cheaper add-ons now or proceed without them.

children.label: Review and commit the booking
children.note: 8.1 with 8.2 against it. 8.3 whenever the platform moves the price mid-checkout - three keepers meet it, at three different spots, with three different outcomes. 8.4 and 8.5 as the screen asks - -dAg answers 8.4 before the passenger form even exists, and the choice changes the price. then 8.6; 8.7 and 8.8 only on the hold path (UiwB). no keeper pays money on camera.

questions.question: Has a session timeout warning appeared indicating you are about to lose your reserved fare and seats?
questions.why: Flight booking sessions usually have strict timers (e.g., 10-15 minutes) to hold inventory, and if the timer expires before payment is processed, you must restart and the price may jump.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that you need to immediately complete the payment or risk having the transaction fail and the fare disappear.

questions.question: Did the page reach a booking confirmation, or did the bank pop-up fail or time out?
questions.why: Airline payment processors often rely on 3D Secure pop-ups or bank redirects that can be blocked by browsers or time out, leaving the transaction in limbo.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty of knowing whether your card was charged and your flight secured, potentially resulting in a lost reservation.

questions.question: Are you comfortable with the current booking total before adding bags?
questions.why: The screen shows a detailed breakdown of fares, fees, and taxes totaling ¥21,270 JPY that should be verified before proceeding to baggage selection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to confirm the base fare and taxes align with their budget before extra add-on costs are introduced.

questions.question: Is the lowest fare actually offered higher than the price the calendar advertised?
questions.why: The date carousel advertised 672,720 NGN for May 14, but the lowest available fare class upon selection jumped to 730,269 NGN.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly accept the higher fare without realizing the advertised price was misleading, causing you to overpay.

questions.question: Does the departure date match the airport arrival warning?
questions.why: The selected flight shows a departure on Tuesday, March 24, but the fare modal explicitly warns to arrive at the airport on Monday, March 25.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to catch a critical date discrepancy that could result in showing up at the airport on the wrong day.

questions.question: Do you accept the new, higher price to continue with the booking?
questions.why: The booking site alerted you that the ticket price increased to 149 € and asked if you want to accept the new fare or select an alternative trip.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If an agent automatically accepts the price hike, you might end up paying more than you budgeted instead of exploring the cheaper alternatives provided.

questions.question: Do you accept the updated fare?
questions.why: The booking site displayed a notification that the fare decreased by ₹ 10 to ₹ 4,985, requiring you to acknowledge the new price before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the dynamic price change and decide whether you still want to proceed with the transaction.

questions.question: Which payment method will you use, and are you willing to pay extra fees for certain options?
questions.why: The screen shows that selecting certain options like Payment Centers adds a PHP 224 hold fee to your booking total.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether the convenience of a specific payment method is worth the extra fee.

questions.question: Should you choose to be billed in the airline's local currency or accept the site's guaranteed exchange rate in your home currency?
questions.why: Booking sites and payment gateways often offer Dynamic Currency Conversion (DCC), which applies a heavily inflated exchange rate compared to letting your travel credit card handle the conversion.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might select your home currency thinking it is safer or clearer, inadvertently adding a 5-7% hidden markup to the final cost of the flight.

questions.question: Are you ready to commit to these non-refundable charges and proceed to payment?
questions.why: The prompt explicitly warns that proceeding locks in the fares and fees as non-cancellable charges, even if the browser is closed before paying.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final opportunity to review or cancel the booking before being financially committed to the charges.

questions.question: Does this booking fall under a 24-hour risk-free cancellation policy?
questions.why: Many airlines and jurisdictions mandate a 24-hour grace period where even strictly non-refundable tickets can be canceled for a full refund.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the knowledge of exactly how long they have to safely reverse the transaction if they spot a mistake or their plans suddenly change right after booking.

questions.question: What hold code and expiry does the page show, and has anything been paid yet?
questions.why: The screen displays a banner confirming reservation XPLKQR is on hold and will expire in 23 hours and 59 minutes, which dictates your payment deadline.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss seeing the exact confirmation code and the specific deadline to pay before the held reservation expires.

questions.question: Does the final confirmation match the 24-hour payment window promised by the Book Now Pay Later option?
questions.why: Checking the expiration time on the final confirmation banner ensures you actually have the promised 24 hours to secure your fare.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying the exact deadline to finalize your payment before the reservation expires.

questions.question: Does the confirmation page say the booking is ticketed, or only reserved until payment?
questions.why: The email explicitly states that the booking is not yet ticketed and provides specific options to complete your payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the emailed payment instructions and verify the exact ticketing status of your reservation.

questions.question: After booking, what does the confirmation page show?
questions.why: Checking the attached itinerary PDF confirms that the booking status is officially confirmed and the passenger details are accurate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate peace of mind of personally verifying the confirmed status and passenger details on the official itinerary receipt.

gamedev.task: build a small playable game or mechanic in a game engine (Roblox Studio, Scratch, Unity, Godot, GDevelop, Construct): start a project, build or place the scene — terrain, platforms, sprites, objects — then give it behaviour by scripting or wiring events, set the rules and values that make it work (speed, gravity, score, spawn, win and lose conditions), PLAYTEST it by running the game, then tune those values against what happened when you played, and publish or export it; complete when the game is published, exported, or shown running as intended. Surface pinned: the editor session that produces one playable thing. The distinctive decision here is the playtest loop: unlike every other creative domain in this set, the maker runs the artifact to find out whether it is right, then goes back and changes a number. Capture that loop, including what they noticed while playing. Off-task: gameplay, let's-plays and reviews of finished games, asset-pack and marketplace showcases, engine or hardware comparisons, game-design theory with no editor on screen, and monetisation or publishing-business advice.

tree.label: Build and playtest a small game
tree.note: 1 first, and 1.5 to 1.8 whenever the editor gets in the way - Nfpn and rWUb open the panels before anything else. then 2 for each object the game needs, with 3 for the ones that must collide or hold still. 4 for the behaviour, in blocks, in a script file or in an event sheet. 5 when the numbers are first chosen. 6 as soon as there is anything to see, and again after almost every change - eleven of twelve run the game, and q7wl is the one that never does. 7 whenever 6 shows something wrong, and it goes back into 2, 3, 4 or 5 depending on what broke. 8 only in rWUb, which then runs 6 against the published game and comes back through 7 and 8.5.

children.label: Start the project
children.note: 1.1 then 1.2 in every video. 1.3 and 1.4 where the engine asks. 1.5 where the editor's own display gets in the way of the work - three videos change it before starting and one changes it mid-task. 1.6 in the Roblox and Unity videos, which tour the panels first. 1.7 in the Godot videos, which make folders before the first scene. 1.8 where the template or the starter arrives with something to remove.

questions.question: Which version of the Godot engine should you download?
questions.why: The homepage presents several distinct options like the latest 4.1.2, an older LTS 3.5.3, and a .NET version, which dictate the features, stability, and scripting languages available for your game.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose whether your project relies on the newest engine features, the proven stability of an LTS release, or C# support via the .NET build.

questions.question: Is Roblox Studio installed and open, ready for you to start the project?
questions.why: Clicking the green 'Start Creating' button triggers the browser to check for an existing installation or prompts the download required to start your project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose control over the installation process and the ability to troubleshoot if the browser fails to launch the engine.

questions.question: Should the project start as a remix of someone else's, or from empty?
questions.why: Clicking the Remix button on the starter project page ensures you have all the required costumes for later animation steps without having to import them manually.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to build entirely from scratch or use a pre-made template that saves time on asset management.

questions.question: Is the engine's project list open, ready for a new project?
questions.why: The Unity Hub screen displays a blue 'New project' button that must be clicked to begin setting up the game environment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally verify the project's initial configuration, template, and storage location.

questions.question: What will you name the project?
questions.why: Replacing the default 'Untitled-39' with a descriptive name makes the project easier to find and identify later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to give the game a meaningful, personalized title that reflects your creative vision.

questions.question: What will you name the project and where should you save its files?
questions.why: The engine requires a valid, empty directory to store the game's assets, as indicated by the path warning and the confirming green checkmark.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to organize your local file system and establish a personalized folder structure for your future game development projects.

questions.question: Which renderer should you select for your new project?
questions.why: The renderer choice dictates the graphical capabilities and target platforms, with the Mobile option specifically offering fast rendering for simple scenes like 2D games.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this setup means losing the chance to optimize the engine's underlying graphics backend for your specific game type and target audience.

questions.question: Are the Unity Cloud and Version Control options left enabled in the new project dialog?
questions.why: Leaving Unity Cloud and Version Control checked by default ties the local project to Unity's online services, which have storage quotas and potential billing implications for larger projects.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to opt out of a cloud service ecosystem that they may not want or need, potentially avoiding future account limits or unexpected fees.

questions.question: Which visual theme do you prefer for the editor interface?
questions.why: The Editor Settings window offers multiple theme presets like 'Breeze Dark' or 'Light', which changes the overall color scheme of the workspace to suit your visual preferences.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose the ability to customize the workspace to your own visual comfort and aesthetic preferences.

questions.question: What custom display scale do you set for the editor interface?
questions.why: The Editor Settings window includes a Custom Display Scale field that determines how large the interface elements appear on your screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to tailor the editor's visual scale to your specific screen size and personal comfort.

questions.question: Can you see the object list, its properties and the scene at the same time?
questions.why: Understanding how the Hierarchy, Inspector, and Project panels interact is essential for finding and modifying game objects like the Main Camera and Directional Light.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the spatial familiarity and mental map of where your assets and object properties are located within the engine's interface.

questions.question: Are the object list and the properties panel both showing?
questions.why: Navigating the Home and View tabs to open these specific panels ensures you have the necessary interface elements visible to select, place, and modify game objects.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the spatial familiarity of the engine's ribbon menu and the personal preference of arranging your own workspace layout.

questions.question: How will you organize the project files?
questions.why: Creating specific folders like 'scripts' and 'scenes' in the FileSystem dock keeps assets structured and easy to locate as the game grows.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to establish a folder structure that matches your specific mental model or workflow preferences.

questions.question: Should you move the 'audio' folder out of the 'graphics' folder back to the root directory?
questions.why: The FileSystem dock shows the 'audio' folder accidentally nested inside the 'graphics' folder, which needs to be corrected to keep project assets organized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to immediately spot and correct accidental file misplacements to maintain your preferred project structure.

questions.question: Should you delete any placeholder sprites from the remixed project before starting?
questions.why: The screen shows a sprite explicitly named 'Delete Me' with a sticky note explaining it is just a thumbnail, indicating it should be removed to clean up the workspace.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to review the template's initial instructions and manually clear out unnecessary placeholder assets.

questions.question: Should the default readme and template assets be removed for a clean workspace, or kept for reference?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Remove Readme Assets' button and a 'Readme' tab that can be cleared to declutter the new project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice of whether to keep the introductory template materials for reference or remove them for a cleaner workspace.

children.label: Build the scene
children.note: the user runs 2.1 for each object the game needs, then some of 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 depending on where the art comes from - painted in the editor, imported from a folder, or taken from an asset store. 2.5 for the level itself, which in Roblox is more of the same objects. 2.6 on every object, and 2.7 where the grid gets in the way. 2.8 when something disappears behind something else. 2.9 once per game. 2.10 as the tree fills up, and in 9v3G because a script needs the name. 2.11 whenever two objects cannot be told apart. 2.12 only in the two engines that slice a sprite sheet. 2.13 where an object has to exist more than once. 2.14 where the game needs music or an effect.

questions.question: Is there a separate object holding the level, apart from the backdrop?
questions.why: Selecting the paint option from the sprite menu allows you to custom-draw the specific platforms and obstacles needed for the level.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the creative control of hand-drawing the exact shapes and layout of the level's obstacles.

questions.question: Which node type should you create to display the background image?
questions.why: The dialog description confirms that a TextureRect is specifically designed to display a texture, making it the correct component for rendering a background.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose hands-on familiarity with the engine's node library and the knowledge of which specific UI controls are best suited for handling 2D assets.

questions.question: Should you use the provided animated costumes right away, or draw a simple placeholder to focus on coding the movement first?
questions.why: The screen displays 32 different animation frames, which can complicate early scripting if you try to implement them before the basic movement logic works.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the strategic choice to use simplified placeholder art to streamline the initial coding process.

questions.question: Do the sprite and its costume still carry their default names?
questions.why: Renaming the default 'costume1' and 'Resources' to descriptive names in the paint editor ensures the logic scripts will be easy to read and manage later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the creative choice of designing the character's appearance and establishing your own intuitive naming conventions for the project.

questions.question: Are the player, enemy, object and tileset sprites all in the project's folders?
questions.why: Expanding the folders in the FileSystem dock confirms that the player, enemy, object, and tileset sprites are properly imported and ready to use.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of visually confirming that every specific sprite file is exactly where it needs to be before building the scene.

questions.question: Are the audio and graphics folders now inside the project?
questions.why: The screen shows a Windows Explorer window with asset folders next to the Godot FileSystem dock, prompting a choice on how to ingest these files into the engine.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the hands-on understanding of how Godot's internal resource system maps to your computer's local file directories.

questions.question: Is the background image showing on its node rather than an empty slot?
questions.why: The TextureRect node needs a visual asset from the FileSystem panel dragged into its empty Texture property in the Inspector to actually display the image in the scene.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the hands-on understanding of how to use the engine's drag-and-drop interface to connect file assets directly to node properties.

questions.question: Is the character's image showing rather than an empty texture slot?
questions.why: The Inspector showed the Texture property as '<empty>', meaning the character would remain invisible in the scene until the image file was dragged into the slot.

govbenefits.task: apply for a government benefit online or manage an existing claim (unemployment insurance, SNAP/food stamps, disability, Medicaid, housing assistance — state portals and agency sites): work through the eligibility screens and application form and submit, or certify/check an existing claim; complete when the submission confirmation or the claim-status screen is shown. Surface pinned: the government benefits portal itself — not benefit-explainer talking heads without a portal session.

tree.label: Claim a government benefit
tree.note: 1 then 2 every session. then the session's job: 3 once per claim, 4 every week the claim lives, 5 when certifying lapses, 8 once benefits flow onto the card. 6 closes 3, 4, and 5; 7 follows 6. the jobs chain across sessions - 3's confirmation starts the clock on 4, and 4 stays blocked while 5 processes (76Pa).
