children.label: Report the work history
children.note: 3.6.1, then 3.6.2 and 3.6.3 per employer; 3.6.4 loops back into 3.6.1 for each further base-period employer (Or9Z adds one, then flips the gate answer to No). 3.6.5 wherever a free-typed occupation is refused; 3.6.6 where the claim doubles as a job-search profile. 5.4 is this goal's reopen twin, built on the state's wage records instead.

questions.question: Did you work for an employer within the last 18 months?
questions.why: Accurately reporting your employment history over the specified timeframe is required to determine your benefit eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means an agent might incorrectly report your recent work history, potentially resulting in a denied or delayed claim.

questions.question: Is my last employer's information completely accurate before I proceed?
questions.why: The screen displays a summary of your most recent employment details, which must be correct to prevent delays or denials in processing your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify that your previous employment dates and employer contact details were entered correctly before advancing the application.

questions.question: Are your employment details, specifically the reason for separation, correct?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a reason for separation, such as 'Laid Off' or 'Discharge/Fired', which directly determines your eligibility for unemployment benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the ability to accurately report why your employment ended, risking a denied claim or penalties if the wrong reason is selected.

questions.question: How do you calculate your gross wages for each past quarter if you don't have exact pay stubs?
questions.why: The form requires you to enter gross wages for six specific past quarters, which directly impacts your benefit calculation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the estimated quarterly wages accurately reflect your actual past work hours and pay rate.

questions.question: Are the gross wages you entered consistent with your last day worked?
questions.why: Entering a full quarter's worth of wages contradicts your earlier entry showing your last day worked was weeks before the quarter ended, which could trigger a fraud flag or delay your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure your reported income mathematically aligns with your actual employment dates to prevent your application from being rejected or audited.

questions.question: Did you work for any other employers during the specified timeframe?
questions.why: The application requires you to declare all employment between specific dates to accurately determine your benefit eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might not know your complete work history for those exact dates, risking an incomplete application or a penalty for omitting a past employer.

questions.question: Is the second employment-history question actually required?
questions.why: Skipping fields on the employment history page might lead to an incomplete application or a denial of benefits if that information is required.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether omitting specific employment details might negatively impact your benefit eligibility.

questions.question: How do you find and select the correct occupation codes for your job profile?
questions.why: Using the 'Occupation Lookup' button ensures your work history is accurately categorized with the standard codes required for the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally search the lookup tool to ensure the selected occupation code perfectly matches your specific job duties.

questions.question: How many occupations does the page say to give, and how many does it require?
questions.why: The page instructions say to select 'up to 2 occupations', but both occupation fields have asterisks indicating they are mandatory.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might arbitrarily select a second occupation just to satisfy the form validation, potentially misrepresenting your actual job search preferences.

questions.question: How many months of experience and which specific skills should you list for your selected occupations?
questions.why: The screen requires you to input your months of experience for two specific occupation codes and describe the skills that qualify you for those roles.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess your experience level or list generic skills that do not accurately reflect your actual work history and qualifications.

questions.question: What is the lowest acceptable hourly wage and shift schedule you will declare you are willing to work?
questions.why: The state uses your minimum acceptable wage and shift availability to determine if you are genuinely available for work; setting the wage too high or restricting shifts can automatically disqualify you from receiving benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might guess a minimum wage or shift preference that either disqualifies you for being too restrictive or legally commits you to accepting jobs you cannot actually take.

questions.question: How do you answer the eligibility questions about other income, recall dates, and school or union status?
questions.why: The screen requires details on pensions, severance pay, and recall dates, which directly determine your eligibility and benefit amount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that your specific financial details and employment status are reported accurately.

questions.question: Has the page flagged any availability questions as still unanswered?
questions.why: Skipping required fields on the Availability Information page will trigger an error and prevent you from advancing to the next step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to accurately report their specific work availability, which is critical for determining their benefit eligibility.

children.label: Choose how benefits arrive
children.note: 3.8.1, with 3.8.2 read where the card is chosen or is the default; 3.8.3 and 3.8.4 where the form offers them. applications only - certifications touch withholding through 4.7, and D3uH sets 3.8.4 from inside account setup.

questions.question: How would you like to receive your benefit payments?
questions.why: The portal requires you to choose between receiving your funds via direct deposit to a bank account or automatically receiving a prepaid debit card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent decide means you lose control over the specific financial account or method used to access your benefit funds.

questions.question: Did the system reject your bank's routing number, forcing you to either provide a different account or accept a fee-heavy prepaid debit card?
questions.why: Legacy state systems frequently reject routing numbers from smaller credit unions or newer online banks, which can automatically default your payment method to a state-issued debit card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to provide an alternative bank account, potentially getting locked into a prepaid card that charges ATM and maintenance fees.

questions.question: Are you comfortable with the fees and terms associated with the debit card payment option?
questions.why: The screen displays the U.S. Bank ReliaCard fee disclosure, detailing potential costs like out-of-network ATM and inactivity fees that will affect your benefit funds.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally evaluate the debit card's fee structure and decide if another payment method might save you money.

questions.question: Do you want federal and state taxes withheld from your benefit payments?
questions.why: This determines whether taxes are deducted directly from your benefits, which affects both your immediate payout amount and your end-of-year tax liability.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent make this choice means losing control over your personal tax strategy and the net amount of your immediate benefit payments.

questions.question: Did the screen confirm the notice preferences were saved before continuing back to the account home page?
questions.why: The screen confirms your preferences were successfully updated and provides a button to continue to your my Social Security homepage.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate visual confirmation that your account preferences were saved correctly before entering the main portal.

questions.question: How do you want to receive notices from Social Security?
questions.why: You must choose whether to receive only secure online notices or both paper and online notices before saving and continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to decide whether you receive important physical mail or only digital communications from Social Security.

questions.question: Do you want to backdate this claim, and if so, to what date and for what reason?
questions.why: The system requires a specific effective date and a written explanation if you choose to backdate your unemployment claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to provide their specific personal justification for the delayed filing, which is required to process the backdate request.

questions.question: Did the application let you proceed to the next screen without filling in the required reason for backdating?
questions.why: The system advanced to the Employer screen even though the field marked with an asterisk for backdating the claim was left blank.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to ensure their application is fully complete, risking a delay or denial if the agency later flags the missing explanation.

questions.question: Which of the suggested documents do you want to upload now?
questions.why: The screen lists suggested documents like proof of income that you can upload now, though it notes you can still submit the application without them.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether to gather and provide these documents immediately or wait for the eligibility worker to require them.

questions.question: Did the system reject your document upload due to a file size or format error, allowing you to proceed but guaranteeing a manual review delay?
questions.why: State portals often have archaic file constraints (e.g., 2MB PDF only). If an upload fails, the system may still let you click 'Next', but your claim will be delayed for missing evidence.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that their critical proof of income or ID was never actually attached, leading to a surprise denial or weeks of delay.

children.label: Certify a claim week
children.note: 4.1, then 4.2 and 4.3 as the portal interposes them. 4.4, with 4.5 where a No on earnings spawns it; 4.6 as the state requires. repeat 4.4 to 4.6 once per claim week in the session - lVpW and urAf each run two. 4.7 rides on the final week only. 6 closes it.

questions.question: Are there weeks available to certify for benefits, and what is the deadline?
questions.why: The dashboard notification indicates you have weeks available to certify and warns that missing the specified deadline could affect your eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct visibility into your current claim balance and the exact deadline required to keep your benefits active.

questions.question: Should you read the detailed eligibility text before clicking the 'Certify for Benefits' button?
questions.why: The screen displays detailed eligibility information below the notification box that could contain important requirements or updates for your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally review the specific eligibility criteria presented on the screen before initiating the certification process.

questions.question: What fraud rules must I acknowledge to proceed?
questions.why: You must check the box to confirm you understand the penalties for fraud, such as failing to report new earnings, before you can continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the specific legal obligations and fraud penalties you are being held accountable for.

questions.question: Should you read the payment processing details before clicking continue?
questions.why: The page contains important details about direct deposit and processing times, such as a five-day wait, that affect how and when you receive your benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to understand the timeline for receiving your funds and the rules for updating your banking information.

questions.question: Is your contact information correct, or do you need to update it?
questions.why: The screen explicitly warns that you must keep your contact information current, requiring you to verify the displayed address, phone, and email before continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the agency has your most up-to-date address and phone number for critical benefit communications.

questions.question: How should I answer the weekly certification questions about my availability, work search, and earnings?
questions.why: Accurately answering these specific questions about sickness, work search, and earnings is required to determine your continued eligibility for weekly benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might incorrectly report your personal work search efforts or earnings for the week, potentially risking your benefits or triggering fraud flags.

questions.question: Are the pre-filled answers to the weekly eligibility questions correct for your situation?
questions.why: You must verify that the answers regarding whether you worked, refused work, or received a pension during the specified week are accurate before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally verify your weekly activities and income, risking an inaccurate claim being submitted on your behalf.

children.label: Prove the work search
children.note: the state sets the shape: 4.6.1 where the rules need reading; repeat 4.6.2 until the quota holds (iVa7 needs three that count, 2mL- three when the activities are applications); 4.6.3 where the log arrives pre-filled; 4.6.4 where the page invites its own bypassing. absent entirely for some claim types - Jt5q answers a question instead, and xoKC has no log step yet certifies work-search activities at 6.4.

questions.question: Do you need to add more job contacts to meet the weekly minimum?
questions.why: The screen warns that you must report at least three job contacts per week or your unemployment benefit payment may be denied.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to accurately report your specific job search efforts to ensure your benefits are approved.

questions.question: Do you need to review the help text to understand what qualifies as looking for work?
questions.why: The 'UI Online Help' window provides specific definitions for what counts as looking for work, ensuring you answer the eligibility question accurately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the agency's specific definitions to ensure your recent activities actually qualify.

questions.question: What are the application details for this job contact?
questions.why: The screen requires you to specify your interest level, whether you contacted the employer, the date, and the contact method to log your work search activity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to accurately report the specific dates and methods of your personal job search efforts.

questions.question: Are your logged work search methods valid despite the warning to only use the Reemployment Exchange?
questions.why: An on-screen caption explicitly requires using the Reemployment Exchange, but the system's log shows that 'In Person' and 'EMail' contacts were accepted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to clarify if their alternative work search methods will ultimately be rejected and cause a claim denial despite appearing accepted in the log.

questions.question: Do you need to provide work search details for this week?
questions.why: The screen provides an option to bypass the work search entry by clicking 'Next', which is important to notice if your specific employment status exempts you from this requirement.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means an agent might incorrectly skip or fabricate work search records without knowing your actual exemption status or weekly activities.

questions.question: Do you want to withhold taxes from this week's payment or update your contact information?
questions.why: The weekly certification form includes optional questions asking if you want federal taxes withheld from your payment or if you need to update your mailing address.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose direct control over your tax withholding preferences and the opportunity to ensure your contact details are current.

children.label: Reopen the claim
children.note: 5.1 - an expired claim exits to a new application through 3, and employer-issued claim forms exit to the phone. then 5.2, 5.3, 5.4; 6 closes it. 4 stays blocked until the request processes.

children.label: Read the claim status and choose the path

questions.question: Do I need to reopen my claim based on my current notifications?
questions.why: The screen shows a notification that you haven't certified recently and must click the button to reopen your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss seeing the specific reason your claim was paused and the special instructions regarding employer or union claim forms.

questions.question: Has your claim expired, requiring you to file a new claim instead of reopening the old one?
questions.why: The dashboard notification explicitly states the claim has expired, which changes the required action from simply certifying or reopening to filing a completely new claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might try to certify for weeks on an expired claim, wasting time or causing confusion, instead of realizing a new application is required.

questions.question: How should you answer the eligibility questions regarding other income and specific employment situations?
questions.why: The application requires you to declare any expected Workers' Compensation or other employer income and clarify if your unemployment is due to a trade dispute to determine your benefit eligibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might incorrectly report your other income sources or mischaracterize the exact reason for your unemployment, potentially jeopardizing your claim.

questions.question: Should you save your application as a draft to finish later?
questions.why: The narrator explains that clicking the 'Save as Draft' button preserves your progress until Saturday at 11:59 pm PST if you need to step away to gather more information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide when to pause the application and the awareness of the strict Saturday deadline to resume before your data is deleted.

children.label: Identify the last employer from the records

questions.question: Which employer from the provided list should I select as my last employer?
questions.why: The agency requires you to accurately identify the very last employer you performed work for, regardless of whether the job was full-time, part-time, or temporary.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the exact final employer is selected, which is critical if you recently juggled multiple temporary or part-time jobs that an agent might confuse.

questions.question: What is your last employer's state ID number?
questions.why: The system requires the 8-digit state ID number from box 15 of your W-2 to search for and link your last employer to your claim.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to directly provide the exact state ID number from your personal W-2, which ensures the correct employer is linked to your claim.

children.label: Attest and submit
children.note: 6.1 with 6.2 against it, then 6.3, 6.4, 6.5 - the states vary the signature, never the order. entered from 3, 4, or 5. five keepers stop at or inside this goal: Or9Z, a0_z, and urAf end before 6.5, q2an never reaches it, and 802J presses it with the result unshown.

questions.question: Are your claim summary answers correct, and do you agree to the legal certification terms under penalty of perjury?
questions.why: This matters because the screen requires you to review your eligibility and income summaries and legally certify that the information is correct.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally verify the accuracy of your claim details before legally binding yourself to the certification terms.

questions.question: Are you ready to proceed to the final review and submit section?
questions.why: The screen indicates you have completed the previous sections and offers the choice to save and exit or start the final review.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether to pause your application or proceed immediately to the final review.

questions.question: How do you safely return to a previous section to fix a mistake you spotted on the summary page?
questions.why: If you find an error in your previous answers, you must find the portal's internal 'Edit' buttons rather than using the browser's back button, which often clears the entire form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to safely correct their own earlier mistake without risking the destruction of their current session state.

children.label: Check the answers against the earlier screens

questions.question: Do the gross wages and hours on the summary match what you earned?
questions.why: The summary page displays $100.00 in gross wages for 10 hours worked, and verifying this implied $10.00 hourly rate ensures your benefits are calculated correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the opportunity to catch data-entry errors in your reported wages or hours that could result in claim denial or overpayment penalties.

questions.question: Does the summary table include all the job contacts you listed on the previous screen?
questions.why: The summary table dropped the 'Salad Chef' job contact that was just listed, meaning your work search record is now incomplete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to catch a system error that omitted one of your job contacts, which could jeopardize your weekly benefit payment.

questions.question: Are there any fields on the review screen highlighted in red indicating a silent validation error?
questions.why: Sometimes submitting a form fails silently, simply returning to the review screen with the problematic fields outlined in red without a prominent error message at the top.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent just says the page reloaded, the user won't know that a visual-only validation error is blocking the submission.

children.label: Verify and track the claim
children.note: 7.1 then 7.2 before leaving the page - one receipt is unrecoverable once closed (76Pa). 7.3 with 7.4 against it; 7.5 where messages sit unread; 7.6 to leave. 7.3 and 7.4 also open later sessions - certifiers read the same dashboard on the way in at 4.1.

children.label: Read the confirmation and next steps

questions.question: Did my submission go through, and what's my confirmation number?
questions.why: The success message confirms your certification was received, and the confirmation number provides essential proof in case of future payment delays.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing the success message and the opportunity to personally record the confirmation number for your own records.

questions.question: Does the final confirmation match the specific weeks you were initially prompted to certify?
questions.why: Checking that the confirmation screen aligns with the initial dashboard notification ensures that the correct two-week period was successfully submitted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this verification means you lose the direct reassurance of confirming that your specific benefit weeks were officially recorded by the system.

questions.question: Does the receipt popup display the correct application number and date?
questions.why: Verifying the application number and timestamp on the receipt ensures you have accurate proof of your submission if issues arise later.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of personally verifying your application number and saving the official receipt for your own records.

questions.question: Has your request to reopen the claim been received, and when can you next certify for benefits?
questions.why: The Notifications section confirms your request was received and provides the specific date you need to check back to certify for your next available weeks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you might miss the specific date you must return to certify for benefits or overlook important unread messages in your inbox.

questions.question: What is the current processing status of your claim?
questions.why: Checking the status tracker confirms your claim was filed and shows it is currently awaiting an employer response.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose direct visibility into your claim's progress and the specific reason it is currently waiting for review.

children.label: Check the numbers and statuses agree

questions.question: Does the expected payout for the certified weeks correctly align with your remaining claim balance?
questions.why: The dashboard showed a $3,600 balance and a $450 weekly benefit, meaning a two-week certification should result in a $900 payout and leave a $2,700 balance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the system correctly calculated your expected payout and remaining benefit balance.

questions.question: Does the 'What to Expect Next' screen agree with the previous screen about why you won't be paid?
questions.why: The final screen states you may not be paid due to an 'active issue', contradicting the previous screen that said it was just a standard 'waiting week'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An automated agent might miss this contradiction in the confirmation screens, leaving you unaware that there is an active issue holding up your benefits.

questions.question: Should you read your new messages now or proceed to your dashboard?
questions.why: The popup alerts you to seven unread messages that might contain critical updates or requirements regarding your benefits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to immediately review potentially urgent correspondence about your claim before taking further action.

questions.question: Is the session still signed in now that the task is finished, on a dashboard that exposes your benefit documents?
questions.why: The dashboard displays sensitive links to your Social Security Statement and Benefit Verification Letter, making it important to know where the 'Sign Out' button is located to protect your personal information.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the peace of mind of personally verifying that your sensitive government benefits session has been securely closed.

children.label: Manage the benefit card
children.note: 8.1 once; then the hub - 8.2 to 8.4 in any order, 8.5 then 8.6 for a PIN change, each spoke returning to the dashboard. 8.7 whenever self-service dead-ends: the recovery channels are a phone line and an office, not a form.

questions.question: Which EBT card management feature do you want to access?
questions.why: The EBT balances card presents options to view transaction history, view card details, or change your PIN, determining which specific management task you perform next.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent choose means losing direct control over whether to review past spending, check card details, or update your security PIN.

questions.question: Do you want to tap the notification to apply for LIHEAP Preseason since you qualify?
questions.why: The dashboard explicitly notifies the user that they qualify for a specific seasonal energy assistance program and provides a direct link to apply.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent focused only on checking EBT balances might ignore this targeted notification, causing the user to miss out on additional energy assistance benefits they are eligible for.

questions.question: Do you consent to having your information communicated between servers to log in?
questions.why: Leaving the data sharing consent box unchecked keeps the 'SIGN IN' button disabled, preventing you from accessing your account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether they are comfortable with their personal data being shared across servers.

questions.question: What are my current EBT balances, and should I refresh the screen to get the most up-to-date amounts?
questions.why: The screen displays a specific 'Last updated' timestamp alongside your SNAP and cash balances, indicating that you may need to tap the refresh icon to fetch real-time data.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses direct, real-time visibility into their exact available funds and the reassurance of manually verifying the most current balance.

questions.question: Does the EBT card's 'Last updated' timestamp update correctly after you change your PIN?
questions.why: The timestamp on the dashboard jumps backward from 3:42 AM to 3:11 AM after the PIN change, suggesting a caching issue or system glitch.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to notice portal inconsistencies that might indicate your account changes were not properly recorded.

questions.question: Do you want to view all recent EBT transactions combined, or filter them by a specific benefit like SNAP?
questions.why: The screen currently displays a mixed list of both SNAP and Cash transactions, so you must decide if you need to isolate the spending history for just one program.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this review means you lose firsthand awareness of exactly where, when, and how your specific benefit funds are being spent.

questions.question: Are the transactions listed under the correct month headers in your history?
questions.why: The transaction history displays identical November 2021 transactions under both the April 2022 and March 2022 headers, indicating a potential system error.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to spot obvious discrepancies in the portal's records that might require contacting the agency to resolve.

questions.question: What are my current and desired new PINs?
questions.why: You must enter your current PIN and confirm a new one to activate the grayed-out 'CHANGE PIN' button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent choose your new PIN compromises the security and exclusive control of your government benefits account.

questions.question: Did my PIN update go through, and how do I get back to the dashboard?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Success!' message with a green checkmark confirming the PIN change and provides a 'Back to Dashboard' button to resume navigating the portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss the direct visual confirmation that your new security credentials have been successfully registered.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to verify your account but don't have a Social Security Number?
questions.why: The PIN reset screen requires the last four digits of your SSN to verify your identity, but offers a 'No SSN?' link for alternative instructions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to directly manage how your identity is verified if you lack a standard Social Security Number.

graphicdesign.task: create a graphic design in a design tool (Canva, Adobe Express, Figma, Photoshop): start from a template or blank canvas toward a concrete artifact — a flyer, poster, invitation, social post, logo, or thumbnail — customize text, images, colors, and layout, and export or download it; complete when the export/download confirmation or the finished file is shown. Surface pinned: the design-tool session — not design-theory videos, not portfolio showcases. AI-generation flows (Canva Magic Design, text-to-image design generators) are off-task: the arc must be manual template or canvas editing.

tree.label: Create and export a design
tree.note: In most of the videos the user starts by opening the tool (1), and completes 1.3 before 2 when the design needs a file the tool cannot make. 2 fixes the canvas: a template, a blank size, or a page added to an existing file, and 2.7 again whenever the background is retuned. then the element loop: for each element the user adds it in 3, edits it in 4 or 5 depending on the kind of element, and positions and orders it in 6 - repeated for every element in whatever order the design needs, 15 to 40 times per keeper. 7 runs during and after the loop and sends the user back into 3, 4, 5 or 6. 8 only for a design that moves, after the static scene is laid out. 9 exports the file and 9.9 carries it to where it will be used. the task ends at 9.7, or with the finished canvas on screen - in four of the videos the user does not export the file, and three other recordings end before the file appears.

children.label: Start in the tool
children.note: 1.1 where the tool is a choice - one keeper compares two, the rest arrive decided. 1.2 always: the phone keepers find the app in the drawer, the web keepers search or log in. 1.3 before 2 when the design needs a frame, a cutout, or an asset pack the tool cannot produce. 1.4 whenever a price or plan wall appears, at any point in the task.

questions.question: Which app should you open to start designing?
questions.why: The app drawer shows many installed applications, so you must identify and select the specific design tool to begin.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide which installed design application to use for their project.

children.label: Open the tool and sign in

questions.question: Where do you go to download the design app?
questions.why: The app drawer displays numerous applications, so you must specifically locate and select the Play Store to get the required design apps.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the official app store is used to download the design tools safely.

questions.question: Is the store's search open with the design app's name entered?
questions.why: The Play Store home screen is filled with promotional banners and suggested apps, so you must specifically target the top search bar to find your desired design tool.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to discover new or alternative design applications that might be featured in the store's promotional banners or suggestions.

questions.question: Which menu do you go to for the free downloads?
questions.why: The top navigation menu contains multiple categories like 'projects' and 'learn', so knowing to hover over 'libraries' is necessary to locate the starting assets.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means missing the chance to browse other available resource categories like 'cricut' or 'sublimation' that might inspire future designs.

questions.question: Which project link should you click to download the starter pack?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple project files like cards and stickers, so you must choose the correct link to get the summer stickers assets.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide exactly which design project they want to start.

questions.question: Which pricing plan and billing cycle should you choose?
questions.why: The screen displays Canva Free, Pro, and Teams plans, along with a toggle showing a 16% discount for yearly billing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over your software budget and might miss out on cost-saving billing options if the agent selects a subscription for you.

questions.question: Do you want the top download quality if it means creating an account?
questions.why: Selecting the 'Super High' resolution triggered a pop-up requiring you to create a free account and start a trial to proceed with the download.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically sign up for a trial or settle for a lower quality without knowing your preference for avoiding new account creations.

children.label: Set up the canvas
children.note: In 2.1 the user chooses a template, a blank canvas at a preset or custom size, or a page added to an existing design. groceries.task: order groceries for delivery on a grocery delivery service (Instacart, Walmart, Amazon Fresh): search for items, compare options and prices, add to cart, pick a delivery window, check out; complete when an order confirmation with the delivery window is on screen. Surface pinned: the web or mobile-app interface of a grocery delivery service — not in-store shopping footage or a recipe/meal-prep video. Variants: ordering for store/curbside pickup, restaurant takeout, receiving the delivery at the door, and meal-kit subscriptions do not belong.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user overpays for groceries and receives unnecessary bulk items because the agent failed to consolidate redundant cart entries.

questions.question: Is each auto-matched item the food ingredient the recipe asked for?
questions.why: The screen shows the integration incorrectly matching a recipe's request for light sesame oil with a Neutrogena body oil product.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user receives an inedible skincare product instead of the cooking oil required to make their meal.

questions.question: Should you filter the search results to only show organic options?
questions.why: The left sidebar features a nutrition section where checking the organic box narrows down the available strawberry options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to specify their preference for organic produce over conventionally grown items.

questions.question: Which category filter should you select to narrow down the search results?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple category options like "Bakery & Bread" and "Pantry", and applying a filter helps eliminate irrelevant items.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to browse specific store departments and discover alternative products they might prefer.

questions.question: Which item from the fresh fruit section should you add to your cart?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple fruit options with varying prices, including strawberries that have a warning about potential unavailability due to high demand.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to weigh price, quantity, and stock warnings to decide which produce best fits your current needs.

questions.question: Which pita bread should you add to the cart, and how many?
questions.why: The screen shows a high demand warning for the Archer Farms Mini Pita Bread, indicating it might be delayed or unavailable.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to decide whether to accept the risk of a delayed item or opt for a different product without a warning.

questions.question: Are you okay with this item being shipped instead of delivered with your grocery order?
questions.why: The screen shows "Sold and shipped by Walmart" and "Free Shipping," indicating the item will arrive separately via mail rather than with the local grocery delivery.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide if you are willing to wait for a shipped package instead of receiving the item immediately with your scheduled grocery delivery.

questions.question: Do you want to add any of these discounted items to your cart?
questions.why: The screen shows a dedicated savings tab with discounts on items like pistachios and almond butter, offering a chance to lower the overall grocery bill.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to spontaneously browse and take advantage of unexpected deals that appeal to your personal preferences.

questions.question: Which promotional deal on tortilla chips should you choose?
questions.why: The screen displays competing promotions, such as 'Buy 2 For $5.00' for Tostitos and 'Buy 1 Get 1 Free' for Tops, requiring a comparison to maximize savings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether your preference for a specific brand outweighs the financial savings of a competitor's promotion.

questions.question: Which pack size should you select, and should you choose a one-time purchase or a subscription?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means losing control over bulk grocery spending and potentially being enrolled in an unwanted recurring delivery subscription.

questions.question: Which butter should you buy?
questions.why: The screen shows multiple butter and spread options ranging from $3.39 to $5.69, requiring a trade-off between price and product characteristics.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to prioritize personal taste and texture preferences, such as wanting a softer butter specifically for English muffins, over simply picking the cheapest option.

questions.question: Which limes do you want to buy, and how many?
questions.why: The screen displays individual limes for $0.59 each with a default quantity of one, requiring you to adjust the amount to match your needs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over the exact quantity of fresh produce purchased, which could lead to having too much or too little for your planned meals.

questions.question: Should you order the produce by the item or by the pound?
questions.why: The screen provides toggle options for 'ITEM' and 'LB' to specify how the quantity of bananas should be measured before adding them to the cart.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the correct amount of produce arrives, as an agent might select the wrong measurement unit and order far more or less than you intended.

questions.question: Are all the items you intended to buy actually listed in the cart?
questions.why: The cart displayed a total of $34.30 and a specific list of items, but the recently added Evian water was visibly missing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user will not receive all their desired groceries because the agent failed to ensure every requested item was successfully added to the cart.

children.label: Review the cart
children.note: 5.1 then 5.2, with 5.3 as needed. 5.4 or 5.5 whenever the meter shows - both send the run back into 4 (KnrH, uWX7, XBsT), or the shortfall is bought off as a fee (w7tc). 5.6 where offered. rPnc sets its substitution checkboxes here - that is 6 entered from the cart.

questions.question: Are the items and quantities in your cart correct?
questions.why: Reviewing the cart ensures that the quantities and prices for items like the baguette, goat cheese, and berries are accurate before paying the $258.49 total.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to catch missing items, accidental duplicates, or unexpected totals before the order is finalized.

questions.question: Are you ready to check out with this cart?
questions.why: Confirming the $50.04 cart total ensures you are comfortable with the cost before moving forward to the checkout screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify that the total cost aligns with your budget before initiating the checkout process.

questions.question: Should I adjust the quantity of any items before adding them to the cart?

questions.question: Do you need to increase the quantity of cake pans?
questions.why: Adjusting the quantity of the Mainstays Cake Pans directly in the cart sidebar ensures you have enough bakeware before proceeding to checkout.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to evaluate your upcoming baking needs and spontaneously add extra pans to the order.

questions.question: Which items should you add to meet the $35 minimum order requirement?

questions.question: Should you increase the quantity of an item already in your cart to reach the order minimum?
questions.why: The cart subtotal was $24.84, so increasing the yogurt quantity from 1 to 5 was an attempt to meet the delivery minimum.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose which specific items to stock up on when trying to reach the minimum order threshold.

questions.question: Does a delivery fee still show even though the subtotal clears the threshold?
questions.why: The cart prompted to add $0.70 to reach the $35.00 minimum for free delivery, which was confirmed at checkout when a $36.95 subtotal waived the fee.

children.label: Set the substitution policy
children.note: 6.1 where the platform keeps one preference (N5-3, vQTL). per item: 6.2, 6.3, or 6.4 - 6.5 when nothing is suggested, 6.6 where history pre-fills. 6.7 signs off, or skips the whole pass (QeWn). the goal moves with the platform: a running-low popup at the add (qBwH), checkboxes in the cart (rPnc), a dedicated checkout page (UtCH, _5jL), a persistent setting (N5-3), or the whole-order triage right after placing, entered from 8 (rX1S, bpci, QeWn).

questions.question: Do you want to pre-approve any of the suggested replacements or skip this step?
questions.why: The screen shows a list of potentially low-stock items and suggests specific substitutes, like a 2 lb bag of flour instead of a 5 lb bag, for you to approve.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to specify exactly which substitute products you are willing to accept and pay for if your original choices are unavailable.

questions.question: Does the suggested replacement have the attribute the original was chosen for?
questions.why: The suggested replacements, such as the Happy Harvest Fire Roasted Diced Tomatoes, do not include the green chilies present in the original item.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the control to reject an inadequate substitution that lacks a crucial ingredient for your intended recipe.

questions.question: Do you want to allow the shopper to substitute items if your chosen products are out of stock?
questions.why: The screen displays a substitution preferences page warning about out-of-stock items and asking if you want to allow replacements to increase fulfillment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might approve unwanted replacements for specific brands you prefer or reject substitutions for essential items you need regardless of the brand.

questions.question: Are the automatically applied replacement preferences correct?
questions.why: The screen shows previously saved substitution rules, like replacing sour cream with Greek yogurt or refunding muffin mix, which might not match what you want for this specific order.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to tailor their substitution choices for the current order, which could result in receiving unwanted items or missing out on essential ingredients.

children.label: Complete the checkout
children.note: 7.1 as the interstitials appear - one is mandatory (a6v5). the window is goal 3 entered here on Instacart-style platforms, and the empty-calendar wall fires here too (KnrH, a6v5). 7.2 and 7.3 in any order; 7.4 and 7.5 only where the order demands them; 7.6 to 7.8 as payment needs - most keepers ride a stored card or a wallet, and 1.5 is reached back into when the fee-killing trial appears (KnrH). 7.9 with 7.10 against it, then 7.11. seven of twenty-four get through; the rest die at walls this goal owns or stop on purpose.
