questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to negotiate their payment terms, set their own milestones, and review their net earnings before applying.

questions.question: Does the bid field hold the whole amount, without an error outline?
questions.why: The screen showed a partially typed digit in the milestone amount field with a red warning outline, contradicting the assumption that a complete bid was successfully entered.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their proposed compensation, risking an incomplete application or a bid that does not reflect their actual rate.

questions.question: What estimated project duration should you select?
questions.why: The client explicitly stated a preference for a '1 to 3 months Project Length' earlier in the posting, making it the most strategic choice.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to strategically tailor your application answers to match the employer's explicitly stated preferences.

questions.question: Are you keeping your bid amount within the fixed-price budget listed in the job posting?
questions.why: The job posting explicitly listed a fixed budget of $200.00, but a bid of $300.00 was entered on the application form.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses a realistic chance at the job because the agent submitted a bid that ignored the employer's stated budget constraints.

questions.question: What should you write in the cover letter section?
questions.why: The application features an empty text box for a cover letter with a banner offering personalized tips, providing an opportunity to explain your professional background.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing the chance to personally articulate your unique qualifications and professional story in your own voice.

questions.question: Do you want to spend extra connects to boost this proposal before submitting?
questions.why: The screen offers an optional 'Boost your proposal' section where you can bid extra connects to stand out among the current live proposals.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means an agent might waste your limited connects on an unnecessary boost or miss an opportunity to highlight a crucial application.

children.label: Review and submit the application
children.note: 7.1 with 7.2 and 7.3 against it; 7.4 where a declaration exists; then 7.5, with 7.6 riding on the review screen. five keepers cut away or bounce at 7.5 - the submit is the least-witnessed moment in the corpus.

questions.question: Is all your entered information accurate and ready for final submission?
questions.why: The screen displays a comprehensive review page with a banner stating the application is incomplete until submitted, making this the final opportunity to catch any errors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally verify that their personal details, eligibility answers, and attached documents are perfectly accurate before finalizing the application.

questions.question: Do your questionnaire answers match the experience listed on your resume?
questions.why: The review screen shows a contradiction between the 7 and 10+ years of experience on the resume and the 8 and 12 years claimed in the questionnaire, which could cause the employer to reject the application.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to catch and correct inconsistencies between their uploaded documents and form answers before the employer sees them.

questions.question: Does the job ID and location on the application form match the posting you originally selected?
questions.why: The application form header displays a Kolkata role with Job ID [number], contradicting the Delhi role with Job ID [number] that was reviewed on the job description page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to secure their desired position if the agent blindly submits an application for the wrong location and job ID.

questions.question: Do you agree to the legal declaration certifying the truthfulness of your application?
questions.why: The declaration modal explicitly warns that providing false or fraudulent information can be grounds for dismissal or not being hired.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step removes your ability to personally attest to the accuracy of your application before accepting legal liability for its contents.

questions.question: Should you keep waiting for the stalled application to process or abandon it?
questions.why: The application page stalled during submission, requiring a decision on whether to wait indefinitely or click the SEEK logo to return to the homepage.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide their own tolerance for technical glitches and when to cut their losses on a stalled job application.

questions.question: Did a confirmation appear after the application was sent?
questions.why: The screen jumped back to the top of the unsubmitted proposal page instead of showing a confirmation message after clicking the send button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that their application was actually submitted and received by the employer.

questions.question: Did you set the email updates toggle to the requested on position?
questions.why: The narrator explicitly instructed to turn on email updates, but the screen shows the toggle being switched to the off state.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses out on desired job alerts and communications because the agent applied the opposite of their requested setting.

children.label: Complete the assessment or verification
children.note: 8.1, then 8.2 or 8.3 as the platform demands. CL48 enters this goal from the dashboard with the application already in; skni reaches 8.1 straight from the wizard and stops there; GPCO's 8.3 restarts from 8.3.1 on failure. the ERA and Indeed keepers never see this goal.

questions.question: What specific tasks do you need to complete for onboarding, and how long will they take?
questions.why: The screen outlines a multi-step onboarding process, including identity verification and a 30-minute assessment, that must be finished to start tasking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally handle sensitive identity and tax setup steps or gauge the actual time commitment required for the project assessments.

questions.question: Do the two screens state the same time for the assessment?
questions.why: The dashboard initially estimated 20-30 minutes, but the 'Getting Started' screen contradicts this by advising you to set aside 15 minutes.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating to an agent means you miss out on spotting this inconsistency, leaving you uncertain about the actual time commitment required.

questions.question: Are you ready to begin the proctored online assessment in a single sitting?
questions.why: The instructions require you to complete the assessment within four hours in one sitting while your video and audio are recorded.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally complete the assessment, which requires your physical presence for video and audio proctoring.

children.label: Take the assessment
children.note: 8.2.1, then 8.2.2 to 8.2.5 in the fixed order, then 8.2.6; no back navigation beyond one question in 8.2.4.

questions.question: What are the rules and instructions for this assessment section?
questions.why: The screen outlines critical constraints for the assessment, such as automatically advancing and only being able to go back one question.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might miss critical constraints like the inability to review past answers or how to interpret specific terms like 'supervisor'.

questions.question: How do you answer the assessment question on screen?
questions.why: This matters because you must accurately report your employment stability by selecting the correct time range from the provided options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this to an agent means losing the opportunity to personally calculate and verify the exact time range that best represents your longest employment tenure.

children.label: Verify the identity
children.note: 8.3.1 to 8.3.3 in order; 8.3.4 loops back to 8.3.1 with a different document; then 8.3.5.

questions.question: Do you consent to Persona's terms for processing your biometric data?
questions.why: The application requires explicit consent for a third-party vendor to collect and process your biometric information to verify your identity.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the privacy policy and decide whether they are comfortable sharing highly sensitive biometric data.

questions.question: The identity check needs a live camera selfie or QR scan the agent cannot perform - does the user take over that step?
questions.why: The application requires access to a camera to verify your identity via a QR code or secure link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An AI agent cannot physically scan a QR code with a mobile device or take a live selfie to pass the identity check.

questions.question: How do you want to handle the identity verification failure?
questions.why: The screen showed a 'Verification Failed' popup stating your identity could not be verified, which might prevent a successful submission.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to troubleshoot the verification error or provide alternative details to ensure the application goes through.

questions.question: What is the final status of your application?
questions.why: The screen indicates that your identity or account is under review, meaning your application is pending rather than fully processed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate awareness that your account requires a manual review before the employer can process your application.

children.label: Track the application
children.note: 9.1 where a confirmation renders. 9.2 and 9.3 where a dashboard exists. 9.4 and 9.5 where offered.

questions.question: What do you want to do now that your application is submitted?
questions.why: The confirmation screen offers options to download a copy of the application, view its status in your dashboard, or return to the vacancy listing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to save a personal copy of the application for your records or immediately review your dashboard.

questions.question: What does the confirmation page say was submitted, and when?
questions.why: The screen displayed a 'Thank You!' message confirming the successful submission, which proves the application process is complete.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate reassurance of seeing the success message confirming their application was received by the employer.

questions.question: Does the closing date on the submission dashboard match what was shown during the application?
questions.why: The application badge stated the vacancy closes in two days, but the post-submission dashboard stated it closes in three days.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses awareness of a platform inconsistency regarding the application deadline, which could affect their expectations for the hiring timeline.

localsearch.task: find a local provider or place by criteria (Yelp, Google Maps): set the criteria — service, area, rating, price — search, compare candidates through ratings, reviews, photos, and details, cross-check between them, and settle on one; complete when the chosen place's details or contact page is on screen as the verdict. Surface pinned: a maps or local-reviews site/app. Variants: booking the appointment or reservation afterwards, and turn-by-turn navigation, do not belong.

tree.label: Find a local place by criteria
tree.note: 1 runs in every keeper. 2 fixes the area (e.g., the map's own view, a centered location, a typed city, an anchored place, or a route in 2.5). 3 names the service. 4 runs only where a filter or a sort is touched, which is four keepers. 5 reads what came back and 5.7 loops to 3 for a new word or category - three keepers run it three times. 6 compares the candidates, mostly from the results list. 7 opens one and reads it, and 8 checks what it says. 9 is where the choice is made, though nine keepers stop at 9.7 instead. 6.4 can send the task back to 7 for the next candidate. WECH, hJNv and CC-h each do this once.

children.label: Reach the search surface
children.note: 1.1 in every keeper. 1.2 where the app or its version is checked first (QE7Z and hJNv). 1.3 only in the three keepers that touch an account. 1.4 whenever the app opens somewhere other than the map. 1.5 in the six keepers that choose between a search bar, a chip row, a Nearby button or a tab before typing anything.

questions.question: Is the address typed in the bar the right one for Google Maps?
questions.why: The address bar displays 'google.com/maps' alongside a matching autocomplete suggestion, confirming the destination is accurate without needing to click.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to verify the exact URL being accessed before the search platform loads.

questions.question: Has the map loaded, with its search box showing?
questions.why: Verifying the presence of the 'Search Google Maps' box and location settings ensures you are ready to input your specific search parameters.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to visually confirm the starting map context and verify that the correct search interface has successfully loaded.

children.label: Check the app and version fit

questions.question: Should you open this app to find local professionals?
questions.why: The screen shows the App Store page for Thumbtack, making it important to confirm it is the right tool for the task before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to verify the app's relevance and trustworthiness before using it to find a provider.

questions.question: Do you want to install the app, or keep using the website?
questions.why: The Google Play and App Store tabs show the Tripadvisor app is highly rated and available to install, offering a dedicated mobile platform for your search.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the choice of whether to use a potentially more optimized mobile application or stick to the web browser for finding a provider.

children.label: Sign in or stay signed out

questions.question: Do you want to sign in, or stay signed out?
questions.why: The modal presents multiple options like Google or email, which determines how your account is accessed and linked to the platform.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose which of their personal accounts or email addresses is linked to the service.

questions.question: Do you need anything in the profile menu, or should we go back to the search bar?
questions.why: The screen shows the profile menu open with options like 'My Collections' and 'Account Settings', presenting a choice between managing your account and starting a search.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to consult their previously saved collections or adjust account preferences before initiating the search.

children.label: Choose where to start the search

questions.question: Do you want to start from a recent search, a trending category, or a past project?
questions.why: The screen displays recent searches like appliance repair alongside trending categories, offering multiple ways to initiate your search.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to organically browse available service categories or conveniently resume a past search from their history.

questions.question: Do you want the city's overview page, or the listings themselves?
questions.why: The search results mixed a general 'DESTINATION' page with specific 'HOTEL' listings, making it necessary to choose the right entry point for a broad city overview.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to dictate whether the search should start with a broad overview of the city or jump directly into specific accommodations.

children.label: Fix the search area
children.note: one of 2.1 to 2.5 sets it - 2.1 in the map keepers who never touch the area, 2.2 where the map is recentered, 2.3 where a city or postcode is typed or already filled, 2.4 in Ie8R alone, 2.5 in the two route runs and OUD6's stop. 2.6 whenever the map is moved after a search - BCrE twice, and QE7Z where the chip is never tapped. 2.7 wherever a distance or a walking time is on screen, because it is measured from the map's center, an anchor, or the phone, and the interface never says which one.

questions.question: What area should we focus the search on?
questions.why: The map is currently centered on Salt Lake City, establishing the geographic boundary for the upcoming search.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to specify the exact city or neighborhood you want to explore for local providers.

questions.question: Do you set the area by typing it, or by moving the map?
questions.why: The screen offers a search bar, recent locations, and an interactive map, requiring a choice between text-based searching or visual navigation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the intuitive, visual control of manually defining the exact neighborhood boundaries by pinching and zooming on the map.

children.label: Centre the map on your location

questions.question: Is the map centred on your current location before the search runs, rather than on wherever it was left?
questions.why: Ensuring the map is centered on your actual location prevents searching in the wrong region, like the currently displayed area around Kolkata and Khulna.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the assurance that the search results will be conveniently located near you rather than in a default or previously viewed region.

questions.question: Is the map centred on your current location again after it was moved?
questions.why: The map interface allows free panning and zooming, making the top-right arrow icon essential for quickly snapping the view back to the blue dot representing where you are.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the intuitive spatial awareness of manually exploring the surrounding streets and physically orienting the search around your exact location.

children.label: Anchor a place and search around it

questions.why: The information panel presents action buttons like 'Nearby' alongside the palace's description and admission fee, prompting a choice on how to proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the spontaneous ability to decide whether exploring the surrounding area is more valuable than reading further details about this specific place.

children.label: Set the route to search along
children.note: These run in order: 2.5.1, 2.5.2 (XJxr's start is the phone's own location, so nothing is typed there), 2.5.3, and 2.5.4. ZSip and XJxr run all four before any restaurant or station exists; OUD6 runs 2.5.4 from inside directions it already has.

questions.question: Do you want one of the suggested places, or a search for exactly what you typed?
questions.why: The screen displays specific autocomplete options like 'Manchester Airport' and 'Manchester Piccadilly', which might format or narrow the search differently than the raw typed text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to choose whether to rely on the app's predefined location entities or execute a custom keyword search.

questions.question: Which terminal at the airport are you going to?
questions.why: The screen displayed a list of specific destinations within Manchester Airport, such as Terminal 1, Terminal 2, and Terminal 3.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify their exact terminal, which could result in the agent selecting the wrong location.

questions.question: How long is the route, and is there traffic on it?
questions.why: The screen shows a 2 hour 48 minute travel time over 142 miles and warns of current congestion on the M6 causing delays.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally review the travel time, distance, and specific traffic warnings to decide if the journey is feasible for your schedule.

children.label: Open the search along the route

questions.question: Is the search scoped to your route rather than the whole map?
questions.why: Clicking the 'Search along the route...' field ensures you find providers without deviating from your planned 1 hour 27 minute path.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the search is strictly constrained to your preferred driving route.

questions.question: Is the stop added inside the route rather than as a new destination?
questions.why: The dropdown menu lists several route modifications, making it the correct place to select 'Add stop' to include another destination.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the chance to personally customize your travel route with specific errands along the way.

questions.question: Do you want to run the search again in this new area?
questions.why: The map has been moved to show Brentwood and Ingatestone, but the visible red pins are still from the previous search area.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manually define the exact geographic boundaries to focus your search on.

children.label: Check where the distances are measured from
Name the service
children.note: 3.1 or 3.2 in every keeper, and 3.3 whenever the suggestion list mixes category rows with business rows - which is every phone keeper. 3.4 where a recent search is offered; hJNv uses it, jHrC does not. 3.5 only in the directory and the two hotel runs, where the site asks for a detail before it will list anyone. 3.6 in OUD6 alone.

children.label: Type the service and take a suggestion

questions.question: Which of the suggested categories is the one you need?
questions.why: Selecting the most accurate category from the dropdown, such as 'Appliance Repair or Maintenance' instead of 'Appliance Installation', ensures the search results yield providers equipped for your specific problem.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to precisely define the scope of your problem using the platform's specific service categories.

questions.question: Should you use quotes around your search terms to force an exact match?
questions.why: Enclosing the search terms in quotes ensures the results specifically match a 24-hour dentist instead of showing general dental clinics.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to manually apply search operators like quotes to strictly filter out irrelevant general providers.

children.label: Pick a category chip or tile

questions.why: The 'Search along this route' panel offers categories like 'Accommodations', 'Food & drink', 'Services', and 'Attractions' to filter the results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to specify the exact category of stops they need during their trip.

questions.why: The screen displays a mix of specific places and category searches like "Comic Book Stores Search Nearby" as you type.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to quickly pivot their search using the app's real-time category suggestions.

questions.question: Which of these suggestions do you want?
questions.why: The search dropdown presents multiple nearby options like 'Album', 'Pulp's Comics', and 'Declik Comics', requiring a decision on which store to evaluate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user surrenders the choice of which specific comic book store to investigate first from the initial search results.

questions.question: Do you want to reuse a recent search, or type a new one?
questions.why: The screen displays recent searches like 'Boriyakhurd Chhattisgarh', offering a quick shortcut if your current goal matches a past one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might select a similar-looking recent search to save time instead of crafting the precise query you know is needed to get the right results.

questions.question: Do you want one of your saved places, or a new search?
questions.why: The screen displays your saved lists and recently added locations like Dolphin Mall and Wynwood, providing an opportunity to revisit previous candidates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might ignore your saved library entirely or pick a past location at random, missing your specific intent to either reuse a saved place or search from scratch.

questions.question: Which appliance brand needs repair?
questions.why: The screen prompts for the appliance brand to match with the right pros, marking it as important.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify their exact appliance brand, potentially leading to matches with pros who cannot service it.

questions.question: What dates and how many guests should the hotel search use?
questions.why: Setting the exact check-in and check-out dates on the calendar and adjusting the guest dropdown ensures the search results only show hotels with availability for your specific group.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to flexibly adjust your travel dates to find better prices or ensure the room configuration perfectly matches your group's preferences.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user is misled into believing the exact hours were found when the agent only provided generic, unclicked search links.

questions.question: Did the voice search apply the modifier you asked for - nearest, best or cheapest?
questions.why: Using specific voice commands like 'nearest' or 'best' allows the system to instantly generate a filtered list of Italian restaurants with their distances, ratings, and operating hours.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this search means you lose the convenience of quickly adjusting your criteria through natural voice commands to instantly see different filtered results.

questions.why: The filters modal offers options like price ranges, deals, and cancellation policies to help narrow the list to what fits your needs and budget.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally balance trade-offs between price, ratings, and specific perks like free cancellation.

questions.why: The screen offers minimum rating thresholds from 2.0 to 4.5 stars, letting you filter out lower-quality options from the search results.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide how strictly to filter for quality, potentially missing out on good places if the threshold is set too high.

questions.question: Do you need the provider to be open right now?
questions.why: The filters panel offers options like 'Open now' and 'Any time', which determines if the search should be restricted to places available immediately.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether immediate availability is strictly necessary or if you are willing to wait for a place that opens later.

questions.question: Is the list sorted by distance rather than by relevance?
questions.why: The screen defaults to sorting by 'Relevance', but finding the nearest gas station requires changing this filter to sort by distance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to prioritize immediate proximity over the default relevance algorithm based on your current urgency.

children.label: Read the result set

lookup.task: look up a specific parameterized public fact and read off the right value: enter the identifying parameters (a place and day for a weather forecast on weather.com or accuweather, a flight number on flightaware or the airline's site, a route and time on a transit-schedule site, a team for a sports score, a channel for a TV listing), get the result for those parameters, and read the needed value; complete when the queried value for the RIGHT parameters (right city, right flight number, right date, right route) is on screen. Surface pinned: a public information site or app (weather, flight-status, transit-schedule, sports scores, TV listings). Variants: news commentary or analysis videos, storm-chasing/weather-event footage, sports highlight reels, and app "review" content do not belong.

mapnav.task: get directions to a specific place with an online map (Google Maps, Apple Maps, Waze): search the destination, pick a travel mode, review the route options (time, tolls, transit lines), and start navigation or read off the chosen route; complete when the chosen route with its ETA is on screen or turn-by-turn navigation has begun. Surface pinned: the map product itself — not dashcam or driving footage, not travel vlogs that happen to show a map.

tree.label: Navigate to a destination
tree.note: do 1 - five keepers start in the phone's settings and two install the app first. 2 floats: before any destination when the preference is the point (zJVt, HrMd, 4AhB, mo0Q), through the per-route door from inside 4 (obk4, bQbE, kIU1, lYnD), or never. then 3, then 4 - except on desktop, where 4.1's form comes first and 3 happens inside it (7EYu, bQbE, 60tT). rework 4 until the route reads right. then one of three endings: 5 (sixteen keepers start guidance, none arrives on camera), 6 (keep or hand off the route instead - 7EYu, 60tT, ETAP, VO5N, sWXu), or nothing (bQbE, FfFy, HrMd, kIU1, PjID). 7 and 8 are excursions from the main map (PjID, QULM, aGGT); 7.5 reruns 3 and 4 offline.

marketplace.task: strike a deal on a peer-to-peer marketplace (Facebook Marketplace, eBay, Craigslist): browse listings, assess the item and the counterparty's trustworthiness, message or bid/make an offer, agree on price and handoff, and commit — platform checkout or an agreed pickup in the message thread; complete when a purchase confirmation, accepted offer, or agreed deal in messages is on screen. Selling — listing an item and closing with a buyer — is the same ask from the other side and belongs. Surface pinned: a marketplace website or app. Variants: booking a service visit (seeded variant), retail shopping on Amazon-style stores, and apartment hunting do not belong.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses their personal naming convention that includes key details like location, duration, and owner for team visibility.

questions.question: Which tag do you want to filter by?
questions.why: The filter menu contains multiple custom tags like 'Queen's' and 'colleagues', so selecting the correct one ensures you isolate the intended audience.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally decide which specific professional or social circle to target for this commitment.

questions.question: Do you want to message everyone on the page, or only the ones the page says are likely to respond?
questions.why: The screen displays valuable filtering signals like '13 are more likely to respond' and '9 open to new opportunities' that are ignored when bulk-selecting the entire page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the strategic advantage of personalized targeting, resulting in outreach being sent to potentially unqualified or unresponsive individuals.

questions.question: Are the candidates on the later pages selected too, or only the first page?
questions.why: The narrator explains that you must scroll down and use the pagination controls to select the next batch of candidates, even though the action itself is not shown on screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the assurance that the agent knows how to navigate multiple pages to include all intended recipients in the outreach.

questions.question: Did everyone you picked land in the pipeline?
questions.why: The screen displayed a pipeline count of 50 despite showing 53 total candidates, which matters because it indicates that some candidates opted out of receiving emails.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the awareness that specific candidates were automatically excluded from the outreach message due to their communication preferences.

questions.question: Who should you invite to this event?
questions.why: The 'Add guests' field and dropdown allow you to select the specific email address to receive the calendar invite.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over who receives the event invitation and what permissions they are granted.

questions.question: Is the event visibility set to Public, so anyone with your calendar can read the details?
questions.why: The visibility dropdown offers options like Public and Private, which determines whether others can read the meeting details or just see a busy block on your calendar.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might leave the visibility on the default setting, potentially exposing sensitive meeting details to anyone who has access to view your calendar.

questions.question: Can guests change this event, including the time?
questions.why: The screen showed checkboxes for guest permissions, which determines how much control the attendees will have over the calendar event.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether guests can alter the event details, invite additional people, or view the full attendee list.

questions.question: What should you write in the body of the email?

musicprod.task: make music in a music-production tool, without AI generation (GarageBand, BandLab, Soundtrap, FL Studio, Ableton basics): start a project, build a track from loops or recorded/programmed parts — drums, chords, melody — arrange sections, adjust basic mix levels, and export or share; complete when the export/share of the track is shown. Surface pinned: the DAW session itself — AI music generators (Suno, Udio) are OFF-task, as are music-theory lectures and reaction videos. PRECEDENT (2026-09-06): a build step that the video deliberately obscures — blurred, sped up, or cut past — with the omission disclosed on screen is NOT grounds to demote, provided the other build clauses are shown. Set on 6xhZ7OUMhrk, where the mixer opens in plain view and the level adjustments happen inside two blurred, sped-up segments the creator captions as skippable. The auditor pulled raw frames from inside both windows to confirm the blur is real rather than a frame-picker artifact. This matters beyond one video: 23% of the creative corpus has a step obscured this way, rising to 42% in aiimage. Treating it as a bar would cut roughly a quarter of the set for a video-editing convention rather than for anything about the work. Record the gap in the crosscheck instead — "clause not pixel-confirmable, disclosed by the creator" — so a reader wanting only fully-observed runs can still filter on it. Still disqualifying: an interface tour that never builds anything (8PVxIqeDZ7U, nSWNfctv1R0), and a fabricated completion where the claim asserts success and the cited frame does not show it.

tree.label: Make and export a music track
tree.note: 1 first, and its values constrain everything after it - 20 of 26 keepers set a tempo before any sound exists. then 2, 3, 4 and 6 as one loop, run once per part, in whatever order the material needs: rtP_ runs it seven times, 72MF six, and h9eU runs a tempo-matching version of it twice before any arrangement exists. 5 once the parts exist, though MfNv builds its sections before anything else and t14T and rtP_ never arrange at all because every region is looped to the end. 7 after or during 5 - 72MF mixes each part as it arrives, FgFX mixes whenever a melody will not come. 8 last, and 10 of 26 keepers never reach it. 6 can interrupt any of the others.

children.label: Set up the session
children.note: 1.1 where the app has to be found at all - four keepers open on a phone home screen. 1.2 in every video. 1.3 only where hardware or a controller is involved. then 1.4, and 1.5 where the material has a key - 72MF and 7mTq set one before writing a note, pmR1 refuses it. 1.6 before the first recorded take. 1.7 when a recorded take drifts from the beat. 1.8 wherever the tool has to be made readable before work starts, and ht5i and 4m09 come back to it at the end. 1.4 and 1.5 can also be revisited later, and h9eU changes the tempo three times on purpose.

p2p.task: send money to a person on a payment app (Venmo, Zelle, Cash App, PayPal): pick or add the recipient, enter the amount and note, review the recipient and amount at the pre-send screen — the no-undo moment — and send; complete when the sent confirmation / completed payment is on screen. Surface pinned: a payment app or a bank app's send-money screen, mobile or web. Variants: requesting money or splitting a bill (seeded variant), paying a merchant at checkout, and bank-to-bank account transfers do not belong.

patientportal.task: use a patient portal (MyChart, FollowMyHealth, LabCorp or Quest portals, a health system's own portal): sign in and complete one concrete arc — view test results, read or send a message to the care team, view or download a visit summary or medical record, or check in for an upcoming visit; complete when the result, message, or record is on screen. Surface pinned: the portal itself — not symptom research (healthinfo), not appointment booking (doctor), not pharmacy refills (refill).

tree.label: Use the patient portal
tree.note: do 1 - 1.2 once, on a first invitation (L1Mf); 1.3 thereafter. then 2, and from 2 whichever of 3 to 6 the day's task is - each keeper walks one to three, none walks all four. 7 after any commit: 3.13, 5.9, 5.10.4, and 6.5 all hand into it. 4 gates on 3 at some clinics (CkVD: eCheck-In must complete before joining) and not others (fW6G: abandoned with Finish later, and the visit proceeds). 8 as needed and at the end.

photoedit.task: correct and finish a photograph in a photo editor (Lightroom, Lightroom Mobile, Snapseed, Photoshop Camera Raw, Apple Photos, Capture One): open a real source photo, judge what is wrong with it, then work the corrections — exposure and contrast, white balance, crop and straighten, highlight and shadow recovery, spot or blemish removal, and local adjustments brushed or masked onto part of the frame — checking the result against the original as you go, and export or save at a chosen size and format; complete when the export/save dialog is confirmed or the finished image is written out. Surface pinned: the editing session on one photograph — the arc is CORRECTIVE, taking an existing image from flawed to finished. Off-task: building a composite or a layout from multiple images (that is graphic design), generating or extending an image with AI, applying a purchased preset with no further judgement, gear and camera reviews, before/after showcases with no visible editing, and shooting tutorials that never reach an editor.

tree.label: Correct and finish a photograph
tree.note: 1 to get the photo into the editor - 1.4 when the photo arrives already edited, 1.7 only in oiAO, 1.9 whenever a price or a paid feature appears. 2 before the first slider, and again before 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 - the person names the flaw, then fixes it. 3 first when the person needs to crop the photo before placing the masks (QTuO, 29mt), and later or not at all elsewhere. then 4, then 5; after 5, the person may need to repeat 4 if the colour adjustments change the light (oiAO, OSj7). 6 for each region that needs its own fix - after 5 in the Lightroom videos, before 5 in Ao-f, and in Snapseed by painting a global edit onto part of the frame. 7 after 6, or before it where the presenter makes the finishing adjustments to the whole photo first. 8 after every one of 3 to 7 and again at the end. 9 when the person is done - they confirm the edit at 9.1 in nine videos, export the photo through 9.2 to 9.6 in five, and apply the edit to other photos at 9.8.

podcast.task: edit a spoken-word recording into a finished episode in an audio editor (Descript, Audacity, Adobe Audition, GarageBand, Riverside, Hindenburg): import the raw recording, clean the speech — noise and hum, room tone, plosives — then cut it for content by removing filler words, false starts, long silences and tangents, arrange or reorder the remaining segments, set levels so the voices sit together and the episode hits a loudness target, add the intro, outro or music bed, and export or publish; complete when the export finishes or the episode is pushed to a host. Surface pinned: the editing session on one episode. The distinctive decision here is what to cut from someone's speech and how much cleanup is too much, and in Descript specifically the edit happens by editing a transcript rather than a waveform. Capture that. Off-task: making music or beats (that is music production), recording and mic technique with no editing, studio and gear reviews, streaming or live setup, video editing where the audio is incidental, and podcast-business or growth advice.

children.label: Clean the speech

questions.question: Did playback stutter or throw a system overload error after applying the noise reduction plugins?
questions.why: Heavy audio processing plugins can overload the CPU, causing playback to stutter or halt with a transient error message, which means the tracks need to be frozen or bounced before editing can continue.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The ability to catch transient performance errors and realize the system cannot handle the current processing load in real-time.

questions.question: Which quiet section of the audio do you select to capture the noise print?

questions.question: Does the noise print include a breath or a click instead of steady room tone?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the critical auditory check to ensure the noise profile is perfectly clean before applying destructive filtering to the whole episode.

questions.question: Which tool should you use to remove the noise?

questions.question: Are there other segments on this track that you should silence?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the subjective judgment of determining whether a faint background sound adds natural presence or acts as a distraction that must be muted.

privacy.task: change privacy or account settings and verify they took effect (Google privacy checkup / activity controls, Facebook or Instagram privacy settings, TikTok privacy, iPhone app permissions): open the settings, find the specific control (ad personalization, private/public account, location access, activity history), change it, and confirm the new state is shown; complete when the changed setting visibly shows its new state on screen. Surface pinned: the settings pages of a major account or device. Variants: VPN marketing, general privacy-advice talking heads, jailbreak/bypass content, and enterprise admin-console content do not belong.

tree.label: Change a privacy setting and verify it
tree.note: do 1 for the surface holding the first setting. then per setting: 2, then 3, then 4 - with 5 wherever the surface demands one - then 6. next setting: back to 2 on the same surface, or to 1 when it lives elsewhere. repeat until the checklist is done.

children.label: Open the settings surface
children.note: 1.1, then 1.2 and 1.3 for in-app settings. 1.4 when the setting lives on the account rather than the app or device. 1.5 replaces the walk for a web console. 1.6 when a quick panel already holds the control. 1.7 before touching anything on a shared or multi-account device; 1.8 when the surface demands proof; 1.9 whenever prompts land on the way in.

questions.question: Do you need to enter your personal information into this third-party data removal service to complete the privacy checkup?
questions.why: The screen shows an Incogni onboarding form requesting your name and email as part of a sponsored segment, which is separate from the actual platform privacy settings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might unnecessarily share your personal data with a third-party service by mistaking a sponsored advertisement for the required privacy settings menu.

questions.question: Should this setting be changed at the device level for every app, or only inside the one app?
questions.why: The home screen shows multiple apps like Facebook, TikTok, and Settings, so you must decide whether to manage location access through the system settings or a specific app.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the chance to decide whether to manage your privacy globally at the device level or within a specific app's internal settings.

children.label: Go straight to the settings URL

questions.question: Should you use Airplane Mode to quickly cut off all connectivity and location tracking?
questions.why: The Control Center shows the Airplane Mode toggle, which provides a fast but blunt way to disable all network and location services at once.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to use a system-wide kill switch for connectivity instead of adjusting specific privacy settings.

questions.question: Do you need to switch accounts before changing your privacy settings?
questions.why: The 'Switch account' menu shows '[account]' as the active account, meaning any settings changed next will apply to that specific profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the chance to verify which specific account profile the agent is about to modify.

questions.question: Which account's settings do you want to modify?
questions.why: The screen displays multiple family accounts, so you must specify whether to change settings for the organizer or the child account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might alter the privacy settings of the wrong family member.

pwreset.task: reset a password or recover access to an online account (Gmail, Amazon, Facebook, any web login): start from the sign-in page's forgot-password link, prove identity through a second channel — email link, SMS code, or backup codes — set a new password, sign in; complete when signed in, or a password-changed confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: the web or in-app login flow of an online service — NOT a phone's device-unlock, factory-reset, or activation-lock flow. Variants: phone unlock or activation-lock bypass, changing a password you already know, and setting up 2FA do not belong.

tree.label: Regain account access
tree.note: do 1, then 2, then 3; 4 picks the proof channel and 5 runs it; a lost channel at 4.3 or a dead one after 5.7 drops the flow into 6, and 6.3 can loop back into 4 with a fresh contact; 7 where the platform offers a new password - some code paths skip it entirely; finish with 8. 6 is tried one option at a time, in the order the platform offers them

Surface pinned: a recipe site or cooking app's search and save flow. Variants: actual cooking footage (kitchen videos) as the main subject, recipe-development/food-blogging business content, meal-kit unboxings, and "what I eat in a day" content do not belong.

socialbrowse.task: browse a social feed or forum to find specific content (find top or rising posts in a subreddit, open a community's latest discussion, find posts about a topic, sort or filter a feed): apply the right sort or filter, locate the target content, and open it; complete when the target post or discussion is on screen. Surface pinned: reddit, X/twitter, forums, and community sections. Variants: growing-your-account creator content, drama commentary, and social-media-detox content do not belong.

tree.label: Find content on a social feed
tree.note: 1, then 2 - 2 is short for most keepers and long where the handle has to be fetched from a profile or an article. then 3 or 4: 3 alone for the keepers who never type a query - SfAA, d5FK's first half, NQWU, ARbd, mz5g's lists; 3 first and then 4 when scrolling is tried and abandoned - 2GlE, d5FK, pRWM. 4 builds the query, 5 narrows where the platform has controls, 6 reads what came back. 7 whenever 6 says the list is wrong or empty, then back into 4 - opYq twice, T6c1 twice, Wk3C once. 8 when the list holds the target; fourteen keepers stop at 6 with the list on screen and never reach 8. 9 after 8, or after 6 where the list itself is the thing checked - 9.6 loops the task back to 2 for the next target.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the ability to intuitively guess whether the target content was a reply or an original post based on your memory of the context.

questions.question: Should you filter the search results to only show tweets with links?

questions.question: Should the search require a minimum number of likes or replies?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the nuanced choice of whether to cast a wide net for all relevant posts or restrict the results strictly to highly validated content.

questions.question: Does the search the form built match the dates and fields you set in it?
questions.why: Confirming that the dates entered in the modal match the 'since' and 'until' operators in the search bar ensures the platform correctly applied your intended timeframe.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses confidence in the accuracy of the search results if the agent fails to verify that the requested date range was correctly translated into search operators.

questions.question: Was the query actually submitted, or did the run stop with the text still sitting in the search bar?

socialpost.task: publish a post to social media (Instagram, X, Facebook, TikTok): compose the post — text, photo, or clip — add caption and tags, preview how it will look to the audience, publish, and verify it is live; complete when the published post is visible on the profile or feed. Surface pinned: a social platform's posting flow on app or web. Variants: direct messages, editing the video/photo content itself, and growth or algorithm advice do not belong.

tree.label: Publish a post on a social platform
tree.note: do 1 where the platform is new - one keeper installs and registers, the other eleven arrive installed and signed in. then 2; 2.2 re-enters mid-task when the first composer falls short (T1et). 3 then 4 for media posts - except 4.2 runs before 3.2 when the sound must be laid first (rjjj); text posts skip both (MzVy, e4rd, VTiv, 8wOt). 5 where the platform treats the upload as a titled video asset (L9bf, PXXs, MzVy, T1et). 6 and 7 in any order the composer allows - the corpus works them as a hub, opening most options and keeping few. then 8; 9 when a live post exists - four keepers end without one. another post loops back to 2.4 (rjjj's upload pass; MzVy runs the loop once per post type).

children.label: Get onto the platform
children.note: 1.1 to 1.6 only on a first run - one keeper does all of it, the rest just do 1.3. 1.7 fires whenever a feature first touches the hardware, so it can land mid-task (rjjj's camera and mic prompts arrive at record time).

support.task: reach a live human at customer support (Amazon, airlines, banks): start from the help pages, navigate the bot and menu maze, choose the paths that lead to a person, and get connected; complete when a live agent is engaged — a human replying in the chat window, or a call/callback connected to a representative with the flow visible on screen. Surface pinned: the company's help/contact flow on web or app; audio-only phone calls with nothing on screen do not count. Variants: solving the issue through FAQ self-service, and the substantive dispute after the agent is reached, do not belong.

Surface pinned: the web interface of a tax-filing service. Variants: checking refund status afterwards, filing through a human accountant, and standalone refund-estimator calculators do not belong.

tracking.task: track a package or order (Amazon orders, UPS/FedEx/USPS tracking): find the tracking entry from the order — or enter the tracking number on the carrier site — open the status page, read the scan history, and interpret where the package is and when it will arrive; complete when the current status and expected delivery are on screen and read out. Surface pinned: a carrier tracking page or retailer order-status page on web or app. Variants: filing claims for lost packages, and receiving or verifying the delivery at the door, do not belong.

questions.question: Which delivery alerts does the page have switched on?

tutoring.task: find and book a tutor on a tutoring platform (Preply, Wyzant, italki, Varsity Tutors, Cambly, Outschool): search by subject or language, compare tutors on rates, reviews, and intro videos, pick one, and book or schedule a trial or lesson through to the booking confirmation; complete when the booked-lesson confirmation is on screen. Surface pinned: the CLIENT-side booking flow — tutor-side content (how to become a tutor, earnings) is off-task.

tree.label: Find and book a tutor
tree.note: 1 where the platform demands an account - at the door (jHfA, i3ok, XyTV, KIjj, cDu8, 7RrY), or only when the booking button is pressed (CWIs, cDu8's email gate, 7jo_'s verify wall); half the keepers arrive signed in. 2 before any lesson on the credit platforms (jHfA, i3ok), when the wall fires inside 7 (jMRd), or after a trial to prepay hours (zym-). then 3, then 4 as far as the user bothers - filters are opened far more often than applied. 5 picks one tutor and 5.5 reads it; a profile that fails loops back to 5.1. 6 configures the lesson, with 6.6 for the time. 7 commits in one of three ways set by the platform: pay from the wallet and wait for the tutor (italki), pay at a checkout (Preply, the plan credit in 7RrY), or send a message request and pay later (Wyzant). 8 reads whatever follows, which on italki and Wyzant is a pending request. two keepers skip 3 to 5 and start on a chosen tutor (htcf, jHfA's recommended shortcut).

children.label: Get into the platform
children.note: 1.1, then 1.2 or 1.3; 1.4 to 1.6 on a new account as the platform asks. 1.7 when the gate fires later, at the booking button - it can interrupt 7. 1.8 on the one keeper who lands on the wrong account type. 1.9 where offered, before the search, on the one keeper who opens settings.

questions.question: Do you already have an account here, or should I set up a new one?
questions.why: The screen requires authentication to view the 40,000+ tutor profiles, offering options to sign up via email or social accounts, or to sign in to an existing account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice of which personal account or authentication method is linked to their tutoring sessions.

questions.question: Does the sign-up page carry the free first hour promotion shown on the homepage?
questions.why: The current signup screen does not explicitly mention the free first hour, so navigating to the homepage might be necessary to trigger the promotional offer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the financial benefit of a promotional discount if the agent defaults to the standard signup flow instead of hunting for the special offer.

questions.question: Does the page promise a credit bonus for arriving through this link?
questions.why: The narrator explained that navigating through this specific link provides a $10 credit bonus when you purchase your first class.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the $10 promotional credit if the agent navigates directly to the platform instead of using the referral link.

questions.question: Is the Facebook account it wants to sign in with yours?
questions.why: The screen displays a prompt asking if you want to continue authenticating with a previously used Facebook account to access Preply.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to use their linked social media profile or a different method to authenticate their account.

questions.question: The new account needs a password. Will you set it yourself?
questions.why: The screen requires a password of 6 or more characters where capitalization matters to proceed with the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose your own secure and memorable password for your new tutoring account.

questions.question: Is the personal-info form marked optional, so it can be skipped?
questions.why: The screen shows an email and personal info form that can be skipped by scrolling down.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice to withhold optional personal details to protect their privacy during checkout.

questions.question: A reCAPTCHA is blocking the sign-up. Will you solve it yourself?
questions.why: The screen displays a reCAPTCHA grid requiring you to identify specific objects to prove you are human and proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally solve the visual security puzzle required to bypass the platform's bot protection.

questions.question: What should I pick for how you heard about them?
questions.why: The checkout form includes a dropdown menu asking how you heard about the platform before allowing you to complete the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to accurately report their actual referral source or give credit to the specific person who referred them.

questions.question: Do you want other learners to be able to contact you for language exchange?
questions.why: The onboarding modal requires you to specify if you are looking for a paid tutor and whether you want to receive language exchange requests.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control your privacy and decide whether your profile is open to unsolicited language exchange requests.

questions.question: Does the dashboard still say your email is unconfirmed after you clicked the link?
questions.why: Although you clicked the verification link, the dashboard still displays a red warning banner claiming your email is unconfirmed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly assume the verification succeeded and fail to resolve the system error that could block the lesson booking.

questions.question: The site sent a confirmation link to your inbox. Will you click it yourself?
questions.why: The Wyzant email contains an orange confirmation button that must be clicked to verify your account and ensure you can receive correspondence from your tutor.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step requires granting the agent access to your personal email inbox, which exposes your private messages.

questions.question: Which email address should receive the lesson confirmation?
questions.why: The screen requires an email address to send the lesson booking confirmation and continue the process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose which email address receives the booking confirmation or to abort the process.

questions.question: This is a tutor account, so it can't book. Do you want a student account made?

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that your current account type is invalid for booking and the chance to decide how to set up a student profile.

questions.question: Is the page on the student side of the site rather than the tutor side?
questions.why: The profile dropdown shows tutor-specific options like 'Insights' and 'Classroom', meaning you must switch to a student account to access the client-side booking flow.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent fails to recognize it is logged in as a tutor, it will get stuck in the wrong dashboard and be unable to search for or book a lesson.

questions.question: Which language do you want the app interface to display in?
questions.why: The profile settings screen includes an 'App language' option to customize the interface text.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might proceed in a default language that you cannot easily read if you need to review the booking later.

usedcar.task: research and price a used car as a buyer: set the search filters that matter (make/model, year range, budget, mileage, drivetrain), browse the matching listings, open a specific listing and check its history and price rating, and get a price estimate or value for a specific vehicle; complete when a specific car's listing with its price evaluation (e.g. good/fair deal rating or KBB value) is on screen. Surface pinned: a used-car marketplace or pricing site (KBB, CarGurus, Carvana, AutoTrader, Edmunds). Variants: car-dealer/dealership-side content, car-flipping or reselling business content, car review vlogs with driving footage, and mechanic-inspection videos do not belong.

The task as asked ends at 7.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might overvalue the car based on an impossibly low mileage figure, failing to apply the common sense needed to spot a seller's typo.

questions.question: Does the savings figure equal the value minus the asking price?
questions.why: Confirming the math between the estimated value and the dealer price ensures the advertised savings are accurate and not misleading.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the math behind the advertised deal to ensure the platform isn't misrepresenting the actual savings.

questions.question: Does the price gauge put this price below, within, or above the fair range?
questions.why: Pricing tools often use a visual gauge or slider to show exactly where a specific price falls within a broader market range, providing context that a single raw number lacks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the intuitive visual context of whether the asking price is at the very top, middle, or bottom of the acceptable market range.

questions.question: Should you swipe through the full image galleries for these listings?
questions.why: The listings indicated multiple available photos, such as '1 of 40' and '1 of 23', which could reveal important details about the vehicles' condition.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to visually inspect the vehicle's interior and exterior condition before deciding which listing to pursue.

questions.question: Do the photos show the features the ad claims?
questions.why: Text descriptions on dealer listings can be inaccurate, so zooming in on the interior photos to look for specific details like a Bose logo confirms the car actually has the options you want.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent relying solely on the text metadata might select a car that lacks the specific premium features you requested.

questions.question: Does the fine print say the price only holds with a down payment, financing, or dealer add-ons?
questions.why: Dealerships frequently list artificially low prices to rank first in search results, but hide stipulations in the description stating the price requires a $2,000 down payment or excludes mandatory reconditioning fees.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user ends up pursuing a car that is actually thousands of dollars over their budget once the hidden stipulations are applied.

questions.question: For a private seller, does the ad say they hold a clean title in their own name?
questions.why: Private sellers sometimes engage in 'title jumping' by selling a car they never legally registered, which can trap the buyer in a DMV nightmare when trying to transfer ownership.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks handing over cash for a vehicle they cannot legally register or insure because the agent failed to verify the legal legitimacy of the seller's title status.

questions.question: How do the two cars compare on boot space and weight?
questions.why: The 'Practicality' tab showed a significant difference in boot size (964 vs 1436 litres) and kerb weight, which directly impacts how much gear you can haul.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally judge whether the smaller cargo space is an acceptable trade-off for your specific daily lifestyle and hauling requirements.

questions.question: Should the specs and running-costs sections be opened?
questions.why: The screen displays a passed basic history check and a highly-rated dealer alongside expandable sections for specifications and running costs, requiring a choice on how deep to investigate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you might miss out on crucial details about the car's long-term running costs or specific features if the agent decides the basic summary is sufficient.

questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the strategic decision to consult alternative valuation tools when local regulations block the primary site's price history features.
